FOUND-001.title: Conduct Foundation Event Storm for Foundation
FOUND-001.description:
Complete the foundation by capturing domain architecture through Foundation Event Storm.

Use these commands to populate foundation.json eventStorm field:
- fspec add-foundation-bounded-context <name>
- fspec remove-foundation-bounded-context <name> [--cascade]
- fspec add-aggregate-to-foundation <context> <aggregate>
- fspec remove-aggregate-from-foundation <context> <aggregate>
- fspec add-domain-event-to-foundation <context> <event>
- fspec remove-domain-event-from-foundation <context> <event>
- fspec add-command-to-foundation <context> <command>
- fspec remove-command-from-foundation <context> <command>
- fspec show-foundation-event-storm

Why this matters:
- Establishes bounded contexts for domain-driven design
- Enables tag ontology generation from domain model
- Provides foundation for architectural documentation
- Supports EXMAP-004 tag discovery workflow

See spec/AGENTS.md "Foundation Event Storm" section for detailed guidance.

FSPEC-001.title: Scaffold the fspec Paseo provider plugin project
FSPEC-001.description: Create the project skeleton the rest of the epic lands in: package.json with the Paseo plugin manifest, tsconfig, build and test tooling, entry module that registers the provider, and a placeholder provider module. No protocol behaviour yet - only a plugin Paseo can load and a test harness that runs.

userStory.role: the fspec-paseo developer
userStory.action: have a loadable Paseo provider plugin project scaffolded
userStory.benefit: every later story lands in a real repo with a test harness that proves the plugin loads and registers a provider

rules.text: The project is a standalone Paseo plugin (not an in-repo builtin): it ships a paseo-plugin.json manifest, a default-exported index.server.ts contribution function, and a server/ directory for runtime code. It is installable via `paseo plugin install /abs/path`.

The plugin registers a provider with id `fspec` and label `fspec`. It declares NO `command` (it does not spawn an executable - it attaches to an already-running daemon), so its availability comes from its `status()` method, not from command resolution.

package.json declares only devDependencies (typescript, vitest, @types/node, @getpaseo/plugin, zod) - Paseo supplies the host runtime at load time. It lists a `files` field covering paseo-plugin.json, index.server.ts, server/, and icon.svg.

The scaffold's provider `connect()` returns a minimal ProviderConnection (version 1, an empty-negotiated capability list, a `send()` that rejects unknown session ids, an `onEvent` that registers a listener, and a no-op `close()`) so the plugin is loadable and testable before protocol behaviour exists. It advertises no capabilities yet - those are added by later stories.

examples.text: The developer installs the plugin into a Paseo daemon with `paseo plugin install <path>` and it appears in the plugin list as a provider named `fspec`.
Paseo calls the provider's `status()` and the scaffold reports `{ available: false, diagnostic: 'no fspec daemon reachable' }` because no daemon connection logic exists yet.
The developer runs the project's test suite and a test proves the contribution function registers a provider and that a connected session can be closed cleanly.

architectureNotes.text: Standalone plugin (not in-repo builtin): paseo-plugin.json + index.server.ts + server/ only. Host types via devDependency @getpaseo/plugin@0.14.0-beta.2 (matches the verified contract doc); no runtime npm deps, no build step (Paseo compiles the TS).

FSPEC-002.title: Implement the fspec wire codec in TypeScript
FSPEC-002.description: Encode and decode the fspec wire format in one audited module: bincode 1.x default options (little-endian, u64 varint lengths, u8/i8 bool, u8 u16 u32 u64 and i16 i32 i64 varints, u32 enum variant indices, externally tagged enums), the Envelope framing, and tarpc 0.34 ClientMessage/Response framing. This is the technical core; it must be traceable to the Rust types that define it and covered by golden vectors generated from the Rust side.

userStory.role: the fspec-paseo developer
userStory.action: have a TypeScript wire codec that encodes and decodes the fspec daemon's bincode+tarpc wire format byte-exactly
userStory.benefit: the plugin can actually talk to a real fspec daemon without a hand-wavy, guess-based serializer

rules.text: The codec uses bincode 1.3.3 free-function conventions: LITTLE-ENDIAN, FIXED-WIDTH integers (u8=1, u16=2, u32=4, u64=8, u128=16 bytes), u64-LE length prefixes for String/Vec/bytes, u32-LE enum variant indices, 1-byte Option tag (00=None, 01=Some). NOT varint.

The codec lives in ONE audited module (server/wire.ts + a focused bincode reader/writer) with a small public surface: encode/decode of Envelope, of a tarpc request, of a tarpc response, and of the FspecService method payloads the plugin actually calls. No general-purpose bincode; only the types on the fspec wire.

Envelope variant indices are fixed to the Rust declaration order: Rpc=0, Event=1, LogEvent=2, WorkUnitsUpdate=3, StatusUpdate=4, CmdReq=5, CmdRes=6, SessionEvent=7, SessionSnapshot=8. A client only ever ENCODES Rpc (0); it must DECODE all 9 and reject/ignore unknown indices with a clear error.

The codec must be validated against Rust-generated golden vectors (hex bytes produced by `bincode::serialize` on the Rust side) for every Envelope variant and for a representative set of RPC requests/responses — NOT only round-trip tests, so endianness/width/field-order regressions are caught byte-for-byte.

Golden vectors are generated by a scratch Rust crate in /tmp (never the fspec repo) that copies the FspecService trait verbatim and applies the same #[tarpc::service] macro, so the macro regenerates the identical 123-variant FspecServiceRequest/Response enums — zero hand-mirror drift risk. It serializes representative frames with bincode 1.3.3 free functions + tarpc 0.34.0 and hex-dumps them into test fixtures.

examples.text: The developer runs the codec's golden-vector tests and each Envelope variant and RPC request/response round-trips byte-identical to the hex bytes the Rust side produced.

The developer imports the codec from a later story (e.g. the daemon connection in FSPEC-003) and encodes a `CreateSession` request and decodes the `SessionId` response without writing any bincode logic in that story.

When a later story hands the decoder a frame whose Envelope variant index is 9+ (unknown) or a malformed length prefix, the developer sees a descriptive error naming the bad index/offset rather than a silent mis-parse.

architectureNotes.text: Module layout: server/bincode.ts (focused LE reader/writer: u8/u16/u32/u64/u128 fixed-width, String/Vec length-prefixed u64-LE, Option 1-byte tag, enum u32-LE variant index, trailing bytes allowed on decode) + server/wire.ts (public surface: Envelope encode/decode, tarpc request/response encode/decode, FspecService payloads for the 12 plugin-used methods). Aligns with FSPEC-001 scaffold conventions (ESM, zod-free plain TS in server/).

Golden vectors: scratch crate /tmp/fspec-golden (outside both repos) depends on bincode 1.3.3, tarpc 0.34.0 (full features), and codelet-rpc-types via path. It copies the 123-method FspecService trait verbatim from rust/rpc/src/lib.rs (lines 68-716, commit 626eee1e) and applies #[tarpc::service] so the macro regenerates the identical FspecServiceRequest/Response enums. main.rs serializes: all 9 Envelope variants (mirror enum with real rpc-types payloads), the CreateSession request (id=0, deadline 10s) + SessionId response, plus SendInput/Interrupt/Health/GetSessionStatus/GetModelInfo/GetThinkingLevel/ListProviders/SetSessionModel/SetThinkingLevel/SendInputWithThinking/DestroySession requests and their responses; prints hex lines captured into test/golden/*.hex. The fspec repo is NEVER modified.

FSPEC-003.title: Discover and connect to the fspec daemon
FSPEC-003.description: Attach to a running fspec daemon as a client: daemon.json autodiscovery, an explicit connect URL from provider configuration, loopback-only enforcement, connect/handshake, clean shutdown when Paseo unloads the plugin, and a useful availability diagnostic when no daemon is reachable.

userStory.role: the fspec-paseo developer (and the Paseo user who relies on the plugin)
userStory.action: attach to a running fspec daemon as a client — discovering it via daemon.json or an explicit connect URL, enforcing loopback-only targets, completing the connect/handshake, and shutting down cleanly when Paseo unloads the plugin
userStory.benefit: the provider can report truthful daemon availability and later stories (catalog, session lifecycle, transcript) have a real connection to build on

rules.text: daemon.json autodiscovery resolution order: if env XDG_RUNTIME_DIR is set and non-empty, use $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fspec/daemon.json; otherwise ~/.fspec/daemon.json. The daemon writes it atomically after bind; the client shares this exact resolution.

daemon.json verification: parse JSON, require `port` (u16) and `pid` (u32); `started_at`/`version`/`workspace` are optional. Probe the pid for liveness (kill(pid,0) on unix, EPERM counts as alive). If the pid is dead, the stale file is DELETED and the error is 'no daemon.json found (stale daemon.json removed at <path>) — start fspec daemon first'. Missing file → 'no daemon.json found at <path> — start fspec daemon first'.

Loopback-only: the daemon connection target's host must be exactly 127.0.0.1, ::1, or localhost (bracketed IPv6 allowed). Any other host (e.g. 8.8.8.8, an external hostname) is REJECTED as non-loopback — the plugin never connects to a non-loopback daemon address, because the daemon itself only binds loopback (auth/TLS for external binds is out of scope). This applies to both the explicit connect URL and the port discovered via daemon.json.

Connect URL precedence: an explicit connect URL (provider configuration, env FSPEC_DAEMON_URL) bypasses daemon.json autodiscovery entirely. If the URL is set, it wins; only when it is unset/empty does the plugin fall back to daemon.json autodiscovery.

Target URL shape: for the standard surface the client connects to ws://127.0.0.1:<port> (path /). The port comes from daemon.json autodiscovery or the explicit connect URL. The client always uses the full surface (path /), never /fspec-read-v2.

Connect/handshake: the client opens a WebSocket to the resolved loopback target with path / (full surface). After the WS upgrade the server immediately sends two initial frames — a WorkUnitsUpdate (initial snapshot, may be empty) then a SessionSnapshot (sent even when empty). The connection is considered ESTABLISHED only once BOTH initial frames have been received. An empty SessionSnapshot is valid and distinguishes 'checked, none open' from 'never asked'.

Connection-drop handling: if the WebSocket is closed by the server or the network mid-session (including a server Close{code:1001, going_away}), the client transitions to a connection-lost state, tears down all in-flight/outstanding request state, and the provider surfaces it as a connection loss (open sessions are torn down). The client does NOT auto-reconnect: it stays down until status()/connect() is called again and re-resolves the target.

Clean shutdown: when Paseo unloads the plugin / calls close(), the client closes the WebSocket connection (sends a Close frame / aborts) and releases ALL state — clears open sessions, disconnects event listeners, and cancels any in-flight request tracking. close() is idempotent (a second call is a no-op that does not throw). No sockets, timers, or listener registrations leak after close().

Discovery order (status/connect): (1) explicit connect URL from provider configuration (env FSPEC_DAEMON_URL) — if set and non-empty, use it (after loopback validation) and skip daemon.json entirely; (2) otherwise resolve daemon.json (XDG_RUNTIME_DIR first, then ~/.fspec) and verify port+pid; (3) if neither yields a usable loopback target, report unavailable with a diagnostic naming the missing piece.

Availability diagnostic: when status() is unavailable, the diagnostic must be user-actionable and name WHAT is wrong, distinguishing at least: (a) no daemon.json found / no daemon running (point to the resolved path and 'start fspec daemon'), (b) stale daemon.json removed (stale file at <path>), (c) the explicit connect URL is not a loopback address (name the offending host), (d) the daemon was found but the connection attempt failed (e.g. connect refused on 127.0.0.1:<port>). An available:false status ALWAYS carries a non-empty diagnostic.

examples.text: daemon.json present and valid (port 41413, pid alive) → discovery yields ws://127.0.0.1:41413/ and a connect() completes the handshake (WS open + WorkUnitsUpdate + SessionSnapshot received), so the connection is established.

No daemon.json at the resolved path AND no explicit connect URL → status() reports { available: false } with a diagnostic that says 'no daemon.json found at <resolved path> — start fspec daemon first'.

daemon.json exists but its pid is dead (stale) → the file is deleted and status() reports unavailable with a diagnostic saying 'no daemon.json found (stale daemon.json removed at <path>) — start fspec daemon first'.

Explicit connect URL (provider config) points at 8.8.8.8:41413 → rejected as a non-loopback target BEFORE any socket is opened; status() reports unavailable with a diagnostic naming the offending host and stating loopback-only (127.0.0.1, ::1, or localhost) is required.

Provider configuration sets an explicit connect URL (ws://127.0.0.1:5555) AND a daemon.json exists pointing at a different port → the plugin connects to the explicit URL's port (5555) and ignores daemon.json entirely.
Both $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fspec/daemon.json and ~/.fspec/daemon.json exist, with XDG set → the XDG_RUNTIME_DIR path wins (port 6001, not the 7001 from ~/.fspec).

A daemon closes its connection mid-session (server Close code 1001 going_away) → the client transitions to connection-lost, tears down outstanding request state, and the provider surfaces a connection-lost event; open sessions are torn down. No automatic reconnect until status()/connect() runs again.

Paseo unloads the plugin while the daemon connection is open → close() closes the WebSocket, clears open sessions and event listeners, and resolves; calling close() a second time is a no-op that does not throw, and no sockets, timers, or listener registrations leak afterward.

assumptions: Design split: status() performs LIGHTWEIGHT discovery+validation only (resolve target, enforce loopback, verify daemon.json pid) and opens NO socket — it is a fast availability probe. connect() performs the real WebSocket open + handshake (WorkUnitsUpdate + SessionSnapshot) and returns the ProviderConnection. Connection failures (case d) surface at connect() time, not status() time.

Testability: the daemon client is built on the FSPEC-002 codec public surface (encode/decode Envelope + tarpc request/response from server/wire.ts). It accepts an injectable WebSocket transport (default: Node global WebSocket) so tests can supply a fake/in-memory WS server or stub transport — no real daemon is required to run the suite.

architectureNotes.text: Client lives in server/daemon.ts on top of the FSPEC-002 codec public surface (server/wire.ts: encodeEnvelope/decodeEnvelope, encodeRequestFrame/decodeRequestFrame, FspecMethodIndex). No new bincode logic; daemon.ts only composes codec + transport + discovery.

Design split: status() is a lightweight discovery+validation probe (resolve target, enforce loopback, verify daemon.json pid) that opens NO socket; connect() performs the real WebSocket open + handshake (initial WorkUnitsUpdate + SessionSnapshot frames decoded via server/wire.ts) and reports established only after BOTH are received. Connection-drop surfaces a connection-lost event and tears down in-flight request state; close() is idempotent.

Testability per assumption 2: the daemon client accepts an injectable WebSocket transport (default: Node global WebSocket) and explicit dirs for daemon.json resolution (XDG_RUNTIME_DIR + home), so tests use a fake in-memory WS transport and temp dirs - no real daemon needed. Discovery order: explicit connect URL (provider config / env FSPEC_DAEMON_URL) wins, else daemon.json (XDG first, then ~/.fspec); loopback-only (127.0.0.1, ::1, localhost) enforced before any socket opens.

FSPEC-004.title: Register the fspec provider and build Paseo's model picker
FSPEC-004.description: Present fspec as a selectable Paseo provider: register the provider descriptor, report availability with a useful diagnostic when no daemon is reachable, and build Paseo's model picker from the daemon's provider/model catalog (list_providers, model entries, thinking levels) with sensible defaults.

userStory.role: Paseo user running fspec agents
userStory.action: see fspec as an available provider with a model picker built from the daemon's provider/model catalog
userStory.benefit: I can choose a model and thinking level before or while working in an fspec session

rules.text: The provider descriptor registered by the contribution function has id `fspec` and label `fspec`, declares no `command`, and its availability comes from `status()` (connection-based), per the FSPEC-001 scaffold contract.

status() reflects REAL daemon availability by probing through the FSPEC-003 daemon client: when the daemon is reachable it returns { available: true }; when unreachable it returns { available: false, diagnostic } where the diagnostic names the missing piece (e.g. 'no fspec daemon reachable' / 'no daemon.json found ... start fspec daemon first'), never a bare boolean with no guidance.

The catalog for a `catalog` input is built from the daemon's `list_providers` RPC (idx 28, returns Vec<ProviderInfo>): each ProviderInfo becomes one group of models; each ModelEntry becomes a ProviderModel with id = `<provider.key>/<entry.id>`, label = entry.display_name, contextWindowMaxTokens = entry.context_window. Model ids map 1:1 into Paseo catalog ids — no renaming or derivation beyond the key/entry.id join.

The model picker catalog is built from the daemon's list_providers RPC (FspecMethodIndex 28) via the FSPEC-003 daemon client; the provider's catalog input handler replies with exactly one catalog event carrying the requested requestId

Providers flagged `is_unreachable: true` in the daemon's `list_providers` response are excluded from the catalog (their models are not offered as selectable); a provider with zero reachable providers yields an empty model list, not an error.

Thinking levels are GLOBAL on the wire (ThinkingLevel: Off=0, Low=1, Medium=2, High=3, default Off) not per-model, so the catalog publishes them once at catalog level: thinkingOptions = [{id:'off'},{id:'low'},{id:'medium'},{id:'high'}] with defaultThinkingOption = 'off'; models carry no per-model thinkingOptions.

Default selection: the first model entry of the first reachable provider is marked isDefault and set as defaultModel in the catalog; the global defaultThinkingOption is 'off' (ThinkingLevel #[default] Off). When get_thinking_level is unavailable, 'off' is used and no per-model defaultThinkingOptionId is emitted

When the daemon is unreachable the catalog input rejects with a diagnostic error naming the missing piece (e.g. 'no daemon.json found at <path> — start fspec daemon first'); it never returns a fabricated/empty catalog for an unreachable daemon. Availability probing (status()) and catalog fetch both go through the same FSPEC-003 daemon client

Availability is NOT polled by the plugin: status() is a point-in-time probe through the FSPEC-003 client (daemon.json resolution + liveness + connect); changes in availability are driven by the connection state (the daemon client reports connect/disconnect), never by a timer-based poll loop inside the provider.

Resolve by the documented wire surface: the verified wire protocol (commit 626eee1e) exposes only set_default_model (idx 30) — no get_default_model RPC and no default-model.json artifact — so FSPEC-004 selects the first model entry of the first reachable provider as the catalog default (already rule [8]). If the daemon later exposes its default model (RPC or a default-model.json artifact), the provider must honour it over the positional fallback; until such a mechanism is documented, nothing is invented — when no reachable model exists the catalog carries no defaultModel.

examples.text: list_providers returns [{key:'anthropic', display_name:'Anthropic', is_unreachable:false, models:[{id:'claude-sonnet-4-5', display_name:'Claude Sonnet 4.5', context_window:200000, supports_reasoning:true}, {id:'claude-haiku-4-5', display_name:'Claude Haiku 4.5', context_window:200000, supports_reasoning:false}]}, {key:'openai', display_name:'OpenAI', is_unreachable:true, models:[...]}] — catalog = models [{id:'anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5', label:'Claude Sonnet 4.5', contextWindowMaxTokens:200000, isDefault:true}, {id:'anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5', label:'Claude Haiku 4.5', contextWindowMaxTokens:200000}] (openai excluded: is_unreachable), defaultModel='anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5'

Catalog reply carries exactly one catalog event: {type:'catalog', requestId:<the one Paseo asked with>, catalog:{models:[...], modes:[], thinkingOptions:[{id:'off',label:'Off'},{id:'low',label:'Low'},{id:'medium',label:'Medium'},{id:'high',label:'High'}], defaultModel:'anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5', defaultThinkingOption:'off'}} — modes stay empty (fspec exposes no Paseo modes)

No daemon.json exists (~/.fspec/daemon.json missing, no XDG_RUNTIME_DIR override): status() returns {available:false, diagnostic:'no daemon.json found at /Users/me/.fspec/daemon.json — start fspec daemon first'} and a catalog request rejects with the same diagnostic text — Paseo shows the provider greyed out with that message, never a spinner-without-hint

architectureNotes.text: Boundary: applying a chosen model/thinking level to a LIVE session (set_session_model idx 29, set_thinking_level idx 39, session.configure) is FSPEC-005, NOT here. FSPEC-004 only builds the pre-session catalog (list_providers idx 28) and the availability probe. Wire shapes: ProviderInfo/ModelEntry/ThinkingLevel per docs/fspec-wire-protocol.md §6.7; catalog/picker contract per docs/paseo-provider-contract.md §3.3 + §6.

questions.text: @human: How is the daemon's default model exposed to clients? docs/fspec-wire-protocol.md lists `set_default_model` (idx 30) but no `get_default_model` RPC and no `default-model.json` artifact (searched all docs/). Supervisor scope says "honor the daemon's default-model.json / first provider's default" — is default-model.json a documented client-readable file (path/format?) shipped with a future daemon build, or should FSPEC-004 implement "first model of first reachable provider" as the default until such an RPC/file exists?
questions.answer: Resolve by the documented wire surface: the verified wire protocol (commit 626eee1e) exposes only set_default_model (idx 30) — no get_default_model RPC and no default-model.json artifact — so FSPEC-004 selects the first model entry of the first reachable provider as the catalog default (already rule [8]). If the daemon later exposes its default model (RPC or a default-model.json artifact), the provider must honour it over the positional fallback; until such a mechanism is documented, nothing is invented — when no reachable model exists the catalog carries no defaultModel.

FSPEC-005.title: Drive the fspec session lifecycle from Paseo
FSPEC-005.description: Open, drive and stop an fspec session from Paseo: create the daemon session on session.open, send prompts with send_input, publish exactly one prompt result and one terminal turn event per prompt, interrupt the running session from Paseo's Stop, apply model/thinking selection per session, and release the session on close and on connection teardown.

userStory.role: Paseo user
userStory.action: open, drive, and stop an fspec agent session from Paseo
userStory.benefit: the daemon-backed agent behaves like a first-class Paseo provider

rules.text: session.open creates the daemon session via create_session (RPC idx 3) and maps the returned daemon SessionId into the Paseo session; the daemon session id is persisted in the session's ProviderPersistence (version 1, data.sessionId) so it survives reopen

session.prompt sends the prompt text to the daemon via send_input (RPC idx 4); when the session has a non-Off thinking level it uses send_input_with_thinking (RPC idx 46) with a ThinkingConfig built from the session's current provider/model and thinking level instead

a successful session.open emits exactly this event sequence in order: session.opened (with persistence when config.persist, restoration 'core', committed config), session.config (committed model/thinking values), session.ready — all carrying the input requestId/sessionId

each accepted prompt publishes exactly one session.prompt_result (result {type: 'turn', turnId}) followed by exactly one session.turn 'started' for that turnId, and exactly one terminal session.turn event (completed / failed / canceled) for that turnId — no duplicates, no drops; a second prompt for the same session starts a new turnId

session.interrupt answers request.completed as soon as the stop is accepted, then calls daemon interrupt (RPC idx 5); the turn's terminal 'canceled' session.turn event is the authoritative settlement, driven by the daemon's terminal chunk (Interrupted / InterruptedWithReason)

on session.open the provider applies the requested model (config.model, 'provider/model' format) and thinkingOption via set_session_model (RPC idx 29) and set_thinking_level (RPC idx 39) after create_session, falling back to the catalog defaults when the config omits them

session.close calls daemon destroy_session (RPC idx 87) with the mapped daemon SessionId, removes the session from the registry, and emits session.closed followed by request.completed; close of an unknown session is a no-op that still completes the request

model and thinking selection are per-session: session.open applies config.model/config.thinkingOption (or catalog defaults), and session.configure applies changes.model via set_session_model and changes.thinkingOption via set_thinking_level for that session only; after applying, the provider publishes the committed session.config and then request.completed

any input (prompt, interrupt, configure, close) targeting an unknown or already-closed Paseo sessionId is rejected with a clear 'Unknown session' error — thrown synchronously for prompt (no requestId to answer) or surfaced as request.failed for request-id inputs

connection.close() releases every open session (destroy_session for each mapped daemon session) without throwing — a failing destroy is swallowed, the connection is idempotent (second close is a no-op), and no events are emitted after close

examples.text: Opening a fresh fspec session (no persistence on the open input) creates a daemon session; the daemon returns id 'fspec-sess-42' and the plugin remembers it, exposing {version:1, data:{sessionId:'fspec-sess-42'}} as the session's persistence. Later reopening (Paseo refresh) with that same persistence reuses the existing daemon session instead of creating a new one.

Prompting a session whose thinking level is Off sends send_input(session_id, 'fix the login bug') to the daemon. Prompting the same session with thinking level High instead sends send_input_with_thinking(session_id, 'fix the login bug', a ThinkingConfig built from the session's current provider/model + level High), so the daemon gets the reasoning config.

A successful session.open (persist=true, committed model 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-4', thinking 'high') emits, in this order and only once each: session.opened (requestId, sessionId, persistence {version:1,data:{sessionId:'fspec-sess-42'}}, restoration 'core', committed config), then session.config (the committed model/thinking), then session.ready (requestId, sessionId). No other open-time events are interleaved.

First prompt: the plugin mints turn 'turn-1' and emits exactly one session.prompt_result {result:{type:'turn', turnId:'turn-1'}} then exactly one session.turn {turnId:'turn-1', state:'started'}; when the daemon's stream yields the Done terminal chunk it emits exactly one session.turn {turnId:'turn-1', state:'completed'} and no further terminal for that turnId. A second prompt mints a NEW turn 'turn-2' (turn-1's terminal is never re-emitted), so each started turn gets exactly one terminal and nothing is duplicated or dropped.

While a turn is running, the user clicks Stop in Paseo: the plugin answers request.completed for the session.interrupt input as soon as the stop is accepted, then issues the daemon interrupt RPC for the session. The authoritative settlement arrives later as the turn's terminal session.turn {state:'canceled'} event, driven by the daemon's Interrupted/InterruptedWithReason terminal chunk — the plugin does not settle the turn itself from the stop click.

Opening with config.model='anthropic/claude-sonnet-4' and thinkingOption='high' makes the plugin call set_session_model(session_id,'anthropic','claude-sonnet-4') then set_thinking_level(session_id, High) AFTER create_session, and the committed session.config reflects exactly those values. Opening with model/thinking omitted falls back to the catalog defaults instead of inventing values.

Closing an open session: the plugin calls destroy_session('fspec-sess-42'), removes it from its registry, and emits session.closed then request.completed. Closing an already-unknown/closed session id is a no-op that still answers request.completed (no error), and the session no longer accepts prompts.

A session.configure with changes.model='openai/gpt-5' on an open session calls set_session_model(session_id,'openai','gpt-5') for that session only (no other session is affected), then publishes the committed session.config reflecting the new model and answers request.completed. A changes.thinkingOption=null clears the thinking level (set_thinking_level Off).

Sending a session.prompt for a sessionId the plugin never opened (or has already closed) is rejected with a clear 'Unknown session' error: it throws synchronously (a prompt has no requestId to answer) and no prompt_result or turn is emitted. The equivalent session.interrupt / session.configure / session.close inputs for that unknown id surface as request.failed with the same 'Unknown session' error (close of an unknown id is still answered as request.completed, per rule 6).

The plugin has 3 open fspec sessions (daemon ids A, B, C). connection.close() destroys ALL of them — destroy_session(A), destroy_session(B), destroy_session(C) are each issued — then clears the registry. It resolves without throwing even if one destroy fails (a failing destroy is swallowed), it is idempotent (a second close() is a no-op), and no provider events are emitted after close() returns.

architectureNotes.text: Session lifecycle module (server/session.ts) sits on top of the FSPEC-003 daemon client (connection + RPC transport) and the FSPEC-002 wire codec (server/wire.ts public surface: encode/decode Envelope, tarpc request/response frames, FspecMethodIndex). A per-Paseo-session registry maps Paseo sessionId -> { daemonSessionId, model, thinkingLevel, activeTurnId, turnCounter, persistence }. Daemon RPCs used: create_session (idx 3), send_input (idx 4), interrupt (idx 5), set_session_model (idx 29), set_thinking_level (idx 39), send_input_with_thinking (idx 46), destroy_session (idx 87).

Turn settlement is driven by the daemon's terminal stream chunks (FSPEC-006 consumes Event/SessionEvent/StatusUpdate/WorkUnitsUpdate; this story owns the turn-terminal mapping): Done(13) -> turn completed, Error(14) -> turn failed (error carries the daemon message), Interrupted(9)/InterruptedWithReason(30) -> turn canceled. Exactly-once is guarded by a per-turnId Map<string, 'active'|'settled'>; a second terminal for the same turnId is ignored. Transient timeline rows are terminalized before the terminal turn event. ProviderPersistence is {version:1, data:{sessionId, model?, thinkingOption?}} so resume restores the same conversation with the same settings.

FSPEC-006.title: Stream the live fspec transcript into Paseo's timeline
FSPEC-006.description: Turn the daemon's server-pushed stream chunks into Paseo timeline snapshots: assistant text, reasoning, tool calls with their results and progress, notifications, errors and compaction, plus token and context usage - each published as a complete updatable item so Paseo derives the live delta. No polling of the daemon.

userStory.role: Paseo user running an fspec session
userStory.action: see the agent's live transcript (text, reasoning, tool calls, notifications, errors, compaction, usage) in Paseo's timeline as it streams
userStory.benefit: I can follow and trust what the daemon-backed agent is doing without leaving Paseo

questions.text: @human: How should fspec tool calls render — rich Paseo detail per known tool name, or a generic detail for every tool?
questions.answer: Generic + shell: a tool whose parsed input has a string 'command' field renders as Paseo 'shell' detail (command, accumulated progress output); every other tool renders as 'unknown' detail { input: parsed JSON input (raw string if not JSON), output: accumulated progress / result content }

questions.text: @human: Within one turn, does assistant text that resumes after a tool call continue the same assistant_message item or start a new segment item?
questions.answer: New segment item: each contiguous run of Text (or Thinking) chunks is its own assistant_message (or reasoning) item; any other rendered item, a UserInput, or a turn terminal closes the open segment

questions.text: @human: Should stream chunks that arrive with no Paseo-started turn (another client driving the same daemon session, UserInput echoes) be rendered?
questions.answer: Render everything for the mapped daemon session, with or without a Paseo-started turn; UserInput becomes a user_message, carrying clientMessageId only when it echoes a pending Paseo prompt with the same text; no session.turn events are invented for outside work

questions.text: @human: Is history replay on session.open (history: 'replay') in scope for FSPEC-006?
questions.answer: In scope: on session.open with history 'replay' for a resumed daemon session, page the daemon transcript via get_transcript_page (idx 117) and publish the replayed timeline items before session.ready

rules.text: Generic + shell: a tool whose parsed input has a string 'command' field renders as Paseo 'shell' detail (command, accumulated progress output); every other tool renders as 'unknown' detail { input: parsed JSON input (raw string if not JSON), output: accumulated progress / result content }
New segment item: each contiguous run of Text (or Thinking) chunks is its own assistant_message (or reasoning) item; any other rendered item, a UserInput, or a turn terminal closes the open segment

Render everything for the mapped daemon session, with or without a Paseo-started turn; UserInput becomes a user_message, carrying clientMessageId only when it echoes a pending Paseo prompt with the same text; no session.turn events are invented for outside work
In scope: on session.open with history 'replay' for a resumed daemon session, page the daemon transcript via get_transcript_page (idx 117) and publish the replayed timeline items before session.ready

Every timeline.item is a complete snapshot: Text/Thinking deltas are accumulated by the provider and re-published under the same item id as a prefix-monotonic extension; nothing is polled from the daemon

Tool calls: ToolCall opens a tool_call item (id/callId from the daemon tool call id, status running, error null); ToolProgress appends output_chunk to the item's output and re-publishes it; ToolResult sets the output to the result content and status completed, or status failed with error = content when is_error
UserNotification maps to a notification item (Info/Warning/Error -> info/warning/error); Error maps to an error item with the daemon message (the turn's failed terminal stays with FSPEC-005)
Compaction: a CompactionProgressUpdate with progress opens (or keeps) one compaction item in status loading; CompactionComplete publishes that item as completed with preTokens = original_tokens

Usage: TokenUpdate publishes session.usage { inputTokens, outputTokens, cachedInputTokens = cache_read_input_tokens } and ContextFillUpdate publishes session.usage { contextWindowUsedTokens = effective_tokens, contextWindowMaxTokens = context_window }, carrying turnId while a Paseo turn is active

Transient rows are terminalized before the terminal turn event: on Done/Error/Interrupted/InterruptedWithReason every still-running tool_call is re-published as canceled and a loading compaction as completed, then FSPEC-005 emits the terminal session.turn

History replay decodes each assembled transcript entry as a serde-JSON StreamChunk (externally tagged, e.g. {"Text":{"text":..}} / "Done") and folds it through the same mapper as the live stream; replay publishes timeline items only (no usage, no session.turn) with timestamp = original.timestamp when present

Replay pages with get_transcript_page(session_id, cursor, snapshot_end, max_bytes 65536): first call cursor None + snapshot_end None, then the returned snapshot_end and next_cursor until complete; a TranscriptError does not fail the open — it publishes a warning session.notice and the session still becomes ready

Item ids never collide with rows Paseo already stored: tool items use 'tool:<daemon tool call id>'; every other item is '<epoch>:<n>:<kind>' where epoch is unique per session.open (so a reopened session never reuses an earlier open's ids) and n is a per-open counter of rendered items; snapshots of one item always reuse its id

A ToolResult with isError true and content 'permission denied' publishes the tool_call as status 'failed' with error 'permission denied'
Interrupted while tool call-2 is still running: the provider re-publishes tool:call-2 as canceled BEFORE emitting session.turn canceled

UserNotification {message:'Rate limited', severity:Warning} publishes notification {level:'warning', message:'Rate limited'}; Error {error:'provider exploded'} publishes error {message:'provider exploded'} before the failed session.turn

TokenUpdate {input_tokens:1200, output_tokens:300, cache_read_input_tokens:800} during turn-1 publishes session.usage {turnId:'turn-1', usage:{inputTokens:1200, outputTokens:300, cachedInputTokens:800}}; ContextFillUpdate {effective_tokens:50000, context_window:200000} publishes usage {contextWindowUsedTokens:50000, contextWindowMaxTokens:200000}

Another client drives daemon session fspec-sess-42 with no Paseo turn active: UserInput 'hi from tui' publishes user_message {text:'hi from tui'} with no clientMessageId and the following Text is rendered, but no session.turn is emitted; a Paseo prompt 'fix it' (clientMessageId client-1) followed by UserInput 'fix it' publishes user_message with clientMessageId 'client-1'

Reopening with persistence {sessionId:'fspec-sess-42'} and history 'replay': the provider pages get_transcript_page and the JSON entries [{"UserInput":{"text":"hi"}}, {"Text":{"text":"hello",...}}, "Done"] publish user_message 'hi' and assistant_message 'hello' between session.config and session.ready, then live chunks continue with the next ids
Reopening with history 'replay' when get_transcript_page returns SessionUnavailable: the provider publishes a warning session.notice naming the transcript error and still emits session.ready

Live: Text 'Hel' then Text 'lo' in turn-1 publish assistant_message {id:'<epoch>:1:assistant', text:'Hel'} then the same id with text 'Hello'; a ToolCall {id:'call-1', name:'Bash', input:'{"command":"ls"}'} publishes tool_call {id:'tool:call-1', callId:'call-1', name:'Bash', status:'running', detail:{type:'shell', command:'ls'}, error:null}; Text 'Done' afterwards opens a NEW item '<epoch>:3:assistant'

assumptions: The daemon pushes Envelope::Event stream chunks for every session to each connected client (no per-session subscription RPC), as the FSPEC-003 client already assumes

Chunks the timeline does not render (SessionStateChange, ProviderWaiting, ResponseAttempt*, ContextSnapshot, work-unit/footer/debug/isolation updates, unsupported indices) are ignored and do not close an open text segment

architectureNotes.text: New server/transcript.ts: a per-session fold StreamChunk -> timeline.item snapshots + session.usage, owned by the FSPEC-005 session registry (server/session.ts handleChunk). Terminal chunks (Done/Error/Interrupted/InterruptedWithReason) first terminalize running tools/loading compaction through the fold, then the registry settles the turn. Replay: server/wire.ts gains get_transcript_page (idx 117; TranscriptCursor/Page/Fragment/Original/Error per rust/rpc-types/src/transcript.rs at fspec 81ee9f15) and a JSON StreamChunk parser (serde externally tagged, snake_case struct fields with the camelCase renames on Text/Thinking/Tool*/Interrupted/ContextFill/Compaction variants); session.open with history 'replay' + persistence pages the transcript and folds entries before session.ready.

FSPEC-007.title: Decode and encode tarpc Result payloads with bincode u32 variant tags
FSPEC-007.description: The wire codec encodes/decodes Result (tarpc Response.message and service Result<(),String> payloads) with a 1-byte tag where 01=Ok, 00=Err. bincode 1.3.3 serializes serde Result as an enum: a u32 LE variant index with Ok=0, Err=1. Every RPC response from a real fspec daemon is therefore misread. Verified with Rust golden vectors generated from bincode 1.3.3.

userStory.role: Paseo user driving a real fspec daemon
userStory.action: have every daemon RPC response decoded correctly
userStory.benefit: the catalog, sessions and prompts work against a live daemon, not only the test fake

rules.text: tarpc Response.message is a serde Result encoded by bincode 1.3.3 as a u32 LE variant index: Ok=0 followed by the FspecServiceResponse payload, Err=1 followed by ServerError { kind: u32, detail: String }
service-level Result<(), String> payloads (set_session_model, set_thinking_level, destroy_session) use the same u32 LE variant index: Ok=0 with no payload, Err=1 followed by the error String
the codec is validated byte-for-byte against golden vectors generated by Rust bincode 1.3.3, not only by round-tripping its own encoder

examples.text: Response { request_id: 7, message: Ok(CreateSession(SessionId { value: 's' })) } serializes to 07000000000000000000000003000000010000000000000073 and decodes to { requestId: 7, ok: true, method: 'createSession', sessionId: 's' }
Response { request_id: 7, message: Err(ServerError { kind: 0, detail: 'x' }) } serializes to 07000000000000000100000000000000010000000000000078 and decodes to { requestId: 7, ok: false, error: 'x' }
Result<(), String> Ok(()) is 00000000 and Err('no') is 0100000002000000000000006e6f; a destroy_session response carrying Err('no') decodes to result { ok: false, error: 'no' }

FSPEC-008.title: Receive daemon frames as ArrayBuffer on the default WebSocket
FSPEC-008.description: The default openSocket factory constructs Node's global WebSocket without setting binaryType, so binary frames arrive as Blob; toBytes ignores Blob and every daemon frame is dropped, so connect() hangs against a real daemon. Found by a live smoke test against fspec 0.10.9.

userStory.role: Paseo user with a running fspec daemon
userStory.action: have the provider connect to the real daemon and receive its frames
userStory.benefit: the model picker and sessions work outside the test fakes

rules.text: The default socket factory sets binaryType = 'arraybuffer' before any frame can arrive, so every binary daemon frame reaches the codec as an ArrayBuffer
A binary frame delivered as a Blob (a transport that ignores binaryType) is still decoded, not silently dropped

examples.text: Against the live fspec 0.10.9 daemon, connect() with the default factory never completed the handshake (frames arrived as Blob and were ignored); with binaryType 'arraybuffer' the handshake completed and list_providers decoded
A transport that hands the client a Blob holding the WorkUnitsUpdate and SessionSnapshot frames still completes the handshake

architectureNotes.text: Fix in server/daemon.ts: the default openSocket sets binaryType; the message handler awaits Blob.arrayBuffer() for Blob data. Test stubs globalThis.WebSocket with vi.stubGlobal so the default factory path is exercised without a real server.

FSPEC-009.title: Resume persisted fspec sessions on reopen
FSPEC-009.description: Paseo refresh closes the session (destroy_session drops it from daemon memory; the manifest stays on disk) and reopens with the saved persistence. The provider only reused the daemon id, so set_session_model failed with 'Session not found' and the reopen was rejected (seen live against fspec 0.10.9). send_input to a missing session is a silent no-op, so a prompt would hang. Reopen must call resume_session (idx 55), which rebuilds the session from its manifest.

userStory.role: Paseo user refreshing or reopening an fspec session
userStory.action: have the provider resume the same daemon conversation
userStory.benefit: refresh keeps my history and the session keeps working instead of failing with Session not found

rules.text: session.open with persistence calls resume_session (RPC idx 55) for the saved daemon session id before applying model/thinking; on success that daemon session is reused and no create_session is issued

when resume_session fails (no saved manifest), the provider creates a fresh daemon session, publishes its new id in session.opened persistence, emits a warning session.notice naming the resume error, and skips history replay
a fresh session.open (no persistence) never calls resume_session

examples.text: Live: open (daemon id 4050903e-...), prompt, close (destroy_session), reopen with that persistence -> previously request.failed 'set_session_model failed: Session not found: 4050903e-...'; now resume_session(4050903e-...) is called first, the reopen reaches session.ready with the same daemon id, and a follow-up prompt runs

Reopen with persistence { sessionId: 'gone-1' } where resume_session returns Err('Failed to load session manifest: not found'): the provider creates fspec-sess-42, session.opened carries persistence data.sessionId 'fspec-sess-42', a warning notice names the resume error, and session.ready follows

architectureNotes.text: server/wire.ts gains resumeSession (idx 55, session_id -> Result<(), String>, same shapes as destroy_session). server/session.ts open(): saved ? resume_session then reuse : create_session; resume failure falls back to create_session + notice + no replay. Source: rust/sessions/src/handle_impl.rs resume_session recreates a non-live session from its manifest (fspec 81ee9f15); fspec-tui dispatch_transcript_recovery.rs uses the same call.

FSPEC-010.title: Fail open sessions when the daemon connection is lost
FSPEC-010.description: When the daemon socket drops (daemon restart, crash, network), the daemon client settles outstanding RPCs but the provider never tells Paseo: an active turn stays 'started' forever and running tool rows keep loading. After a daemon restart the sessions are gone and send_input to a missing session is a silent no-op, so later prompts hang too.

userStory.role: Paseo user whose fspec daemon restarts or drops mid-session
userStory.action: see the session fail clearly instead of spinning forever
userStory.benefit: I know to reopen it, and reopening resumes the conversation

rules.text: On a daemon connection-lost event every open session first terminalizes its transient timeline rows (running tools -> canceled, loading compaction -> completed), then emits exactly one session.runtime_failed whose error names the lost connection and tells the user to reopen

session.runtime_failed is the turn settlement for the dead runtime (Paseo turns it into turn_failed), so the provider marks the active turn settled and emits no extra session.turn for it, now or later

Failed sessions are removed from the registry: a later prompt throws Unknown session, a close completes as a no-op, and reopening with the saved persistence reconnects and resumes the daemon session (FSPEC-009)

examples.text: Session paseo-1 has turn-1 running with tool call-1 running; the daemon socket closes with code 1001: the provider re-publishes tool:call-1 canceled, then emits session.runtime_failed { error: { message: 'fspec daemon connection was lost: server going away (close 1001) — reopen the session' } } and no session.turn for turn-1

After the drop, session.prompt for paseo-1 throws 'Unknown session: paseo-1'; reopening paseo-1 with its persistence opens a new socket, calls resume_session for the saved daemon id and reaches session.ready
An idle session (no active turn) also receives session.runtime_failed on the drop, since its daemon runtime may be gone

architectureNotes.text: server/provider.ts subscribes to the FSPEC-003 daemon client's onEvent; connection-lost calls a new registry.fail(reason) in server/session.ts which uses a new transcript.terminalize() export. The daemon client already reconnects on the next request (connect() opens a new socket when not established).

FSPEC-011.title: Queue overlapping prompts as ordered turns
FSPEC-011.description: A prompt sent while a turn is running overwrote the session's active turn id: the earlier turn never got its terminal (Paseo spins) and both turns were 'started' at once, which Paseo forbids (do not interleave turns). The daemon queues input sent while running (input_tx) and runs each to its own terminal chunk; on interrupt, InterruptedWithReason.queued_inputs lists queued inputs it dropped.

userStory.role: Paseo user who sends a follow-up while fspec is still working
userStory.action: have each prompt become its own ordered turn
userStory.benefit: no turn hangs forever and Paseo never sees two turns running at once

rules.text: A prompt that arrives while a turn is running is sent to the daemon immediately and answered with session.prompt_result { type: 'turn', turnId } immediately, but its session.turn 'started' is deferred until every earlier turn has its terminal, so turns never interleave

Each daemon terminal chunk (Done, Error, Interrupted, InterruptedWithReason) settles the oldest unsettled turn, after which the next queued turn emits 'started' and becomes the active turn for usage and stream rows

Interrupted/InterruptedWithReason carrying N queued_inputs cancels the running turn and the next N queued turns, each emitting 'started' then 'canceled' in order, because the daemon dropped those inputs
If sending a queued prompt to the daemon fails, that turn is failed with the send error when its turn comes (started then failed), keeping order

examples.text: Prompt 'a' (turn-1) is running; prompt 'b' arrives: events are prompt_result turn-1, started turn-1, prompt_result turn-2, and both send_input calls reach the daemon; Done -> completed turn-1 then started turn-2; Done -> completed turn-2

turn-1 running, turn-2 queued; the user stops and the daemon sends InterruptedWithReason { queuedInputs: ['b'], reason: user }: canceled turn-1, started turn-2, canceled turn-2; a later Done emits no terminal
turn-1 running; prompt 'b' is queued but its send_input fails with 'connection reset': when turn-1 completes, turn-2 emits started then failed with 'connection reset'

architectureNotes.text: server/session.ts replaces the single activeTurnId slot with a per-session FIFO of turns { turnId, started, failure? }; settle() finishes the head and starts the next; interrupt chunks cancel head plus queuedInputs.length. Source: rust/sessions/src/background_session/messaging.rs send_input (try_send into input_tx), rust/cli/src/interactive/stream_loop/interrupted.rs (queued inputs dequeued and reported on interrupt).

FSPEC-012.title: Let the daemon derive provider thinking config from the session level
FSPEC-012.description: With a non-off thinking level the provider sent send_input_with_thinking with ThinkingConfig { provider_id, level, config_json: '{}' }. The daemon serializes that whole struct and, for non-adaptive models, parses it as the provider request's thinking settings (rust/agent-loop/src/agent_loop/thinking.rs resolve_turn_thinking), so the model provider receives {provider_id, level, config_json} verbatim and fspec's own per-provider config (get_thinking_config) is bypassed. fspec's TUI sends plain send_input and relies on set_thinking_level.

userStory.role: Paseo user who picks a thinking level for an fspec session
userStory.action: have the daemon apply its own provider-specific reasoning settings for that level
userStory.benefit: thinking works for every provider instead of sending malformed settings

rules.text: Every prompt is sent with send_input (RPC idx 4) regardless of thinking level; the provider never calls send_input_with_thinking

The session's thinking level reaches the daemon only through set_thinking_level (idx 39) on open and configure, so the daemon builds the provider-specific config itself (get_thinking_config: Claude budget, Codex reasoning.effort, Gemini thinking config)

examples.text: Session thinking High on codex/gpt-6.1-terra: prompt 'fix the login bug' sends send_input(session, 'fix the login bug'); the daemon resolves {reasoning: {effort: 'high', summary: 'auto'}} from the base level set earlier by set_thinking_level(session, High)
Before the fix the same prompt sent send_input_with_thinking with {providerId:'codex', level:'high', configJson:'{}'}, which the daemon would forward as the request's thinking settings

architectureNotes.text: server/session.ts prompt(): drop the send_input_with_thinking branch. Update fspec-session-lifecycle.feature scenario 'A prompt uses send_input or send_input_with_thinking based on the thinking level' (FSPEC-005 rule 1 was wrong) so the living spec matches. Evidence: rust/agent-loop/src/agent_loop/thinking.rs, rust/agent-loop/src/thinking_config.rs, rust/fspec-tui/src/app/dispatch_slash_submit.rs (TUI uses send_input).

FSPEC-013.title: Replay history as one final snapshot per item
FSPEC-013.description: History replay folded every journalled delta and published each intermediate snapshot (live run: one reasoning row was re-published ~25 times). Paseo stores the projected timeline, so replay only needs each item's final snapshot; publishing every delta makes long histories slow to reopen.

userStory.role: Paseo user reopening a long fspec conversation
userStory.action: have the history replay quickly
userStory.benefit: reopen is fast and does not flood Paseo with intermediate text fragments

rules.text: Replay publishes each timeline item exactly once, carrying its final folded snapshot (full text, final tool status/output, completed compaction)
Replayed items keep their order of first appearance and the timestamp of the transcript entry that first produced them
The live stream is unchanged: it still publishes every delta snapshot so Paseo can stream text as it arrives

examples.text: Transcript entries Thinking 'plan', Thinking 'ning', Text 'ok', Done replay as exactly two timeline.item events: reasoning 'planning' then assistant_message 'ok'
Transcript ToolCall call-1 (Bash ls) at t0, ToolProgress 'a' at t1, ToolResult 'a b' at t2 replay as one tool_call event with status completed and output 'a b', timestamped t0

architectureNotes.text: server/session.ts replay(): collect folded items in an insertion-ordered Map keyed by item id (first timestamp kept, latest snapshot kept) and emit them once after the last page, before session.ready. publish() stays as is for the live path.

FSPEC-014.title: Share one daemon socket across concurrent connects
FSPEC-014.description: Inside Paseo (0.13.2) a real fspec agent's timeline showed every row three times and reasoning text interleaved three ways ('TheTheThe user user...'). connect() only reuses an established socket: concurrent calls made while the first handshake is in flight each open their own socket, the daemon broadcasts every event on every socket, and each copy is folded into the session again. The extra sockets also leak (the client tracks only the last one).

userStory.role: Paseo user running an fspec agent
userStory.action: see each streamed row exactly once
userStory.benefit: the transcript reads correctly instead of tripled and interleaved

rules.text: Concurrent connect() calls on one daemon client share a single in-flight connection attempt: exactly one socket is opened and every caller resolves with it (or rejects with the same diagnostic)
Each server-pushed envelope reaches the provider once, so a stream chunk is folded into its session exactly once
After a failed or lost connection, the next connect() opens a fresh socket (the shared attempt does not stick)

examples.text: Live in Paseo: 'paseo run --provider fspec "Reply with exactly one word: pong"' produced three [User] rows and a thought reading 'TheTheThe user user user asked asked asked...'; after the fix the same run shows one user row and 'The user asked...'
Three connect() calls issued before the handshake completes open one socket; one Text 'hi' chunk then publishes one assistant_message 'hi'

architectureNotes.text: server/daemon.ts connect(): keep a pending Promise<DaemonConnection>; while connecting, return it; clear it on settle so a later connect after failure/drop starts fresh.

FSPEC-015.title: Refuse sessions outside the fspec daemon's workspace
FSPEC-015.description: An fspec daemon serves the one workspace it was started in (daemon.json 'workspace'; get_workspace_info idx 22) and the RPC has no per-session cwd, but the provider ignored ProviderSessionConfig.cwd. A Paseo agent opened in ~/projects/fspec-paseo while the daemon served ~/projects/fspec silently ran in ~/projects/fspec (its sessions were persisted under that project), so it would read and edit the wrong repository.

userStory.role: Paseo user starting an fspec agent in a project
userStory.action: be stopped with a clear message when the running fspec daemon serves a different directory
userStory.benefit: an agent never silently reads or edits the wrong repository

rules.text: session.open asks the daemon for its workspace with get_workspace_info (RPC idx 22, returns WorkspaceInfo { cwd, git_branch }) before creating or resuming any daemon session
The open proceeds only when the session cwd is the daemon workspace or a directory inside it, compared after resolving symlinks and trailing separators
Otherwise the open answers request.failed with a diagnostic naming both directories and the fix (start fspec in the session's directory), and no daemon session is created, resumed or configured

examples.text: Daemon workspace reported as /private/tmp/ws (realpath) while Paseo passes /tmp/ws (macOS symlink): the open proceeds

Daemon workspace /repos/fspec, Paseo opens an fspec agent with cwd /repos/fspec-paseo: request.failed 'the fspec daemon serves /repos/fspec, not /repos/fspec-paseo — start fspec in /repos/fspec-paseo to use it there'; no create_session (reproduced live with real project directories)
Daemon workspace /repos/fspec, cwd /repos/fspec/rust: the open proceeds (inside the workspace)

architectureNotes.text: server/wire.ts gains getWorkspaceInfo (idx 22, no args; WorkspaceInfo { cwd: String, git_branch: Option<String> } per rust/rpc-types/src/lib.rs:494). server/session.ts open() checks it first. Per-workspace daemons need fspec changes (single global daemon.json); tracked as a card in ~/projects/fspec.

FSPEC-016.title: Surface fspec tool approval pauses as Paseo permission requests
FSPEC-016.description: fspec gates risky tool calls (e.g. its RLCD security engine: 'Bash: RLCD security: P(risk)=0.46 >= promptThreshold 0.45') by pausing the session before the tool runs. The stream only carries SessionStateChange Paused; the question is read with get_pause_state (idx 80, Option<PauseState { kind: Confirm|Triple, prompt, tool_call_id }>) and answered with pause_confirm (idx 77, accept: bool) or pause_triple (idx 78, ApprovalChoice Approve|ApproveSession|Deny). The provider ignored Paused, so in Paseo the tool card spun forever until the user interrupted (seen live: three of four Bash calls in one agent).

userStory.role: Paseo user running an fspec agent
userStory.action: approve or deny the tool calls fspec pauses on, right in Paseo
userStory.benefit: gated commands run (or are refused) instead of the agent hanging until I interrupt it

rules.text: The provider advertises the Paseo 'permission' capability and, when a session's stream reports SessionStateChange Paused, reads get_pause_state (idx 80); a None result emits nothing
Triple pauses offer three actions: Approve (allow, primary), Approve for session (allow, secondary), Deny (deny, danger); Confirm pauses offer Accept (allow, primary) and Deny (deny, danger)

A session.permission answer maps to pause_triple (Approve / ApproveSession / Deny) or pause_confirm (accept true / false); without selectedActionId, allow maps to Approve/accept and deny to Deny/reject

Each pause gets exactly one session.permission_resolved: after the answer is applied, or when the pause ends another way (state leaves Paused, the turn ends, the session closes or the daemon connection drops)
A session.permission for an unknown session is rejected synchronously with Unknown session; an answer for a pause that already resolved is ignored

A pause becomes one session.permission { kind: 'tool', name: the tool name fspec prefixes to the prompt ('<tool>: <message>'), title 'Allow <tool>?', description: the prompt plus fspec's details text, detail: the shell/unknown detail of the session's tool call still running when the pause arrived } with a stable id per pause; PauseState.tool_call_id is NOT an id: fspec 0.10.9 fills it with the pause details text (rust/sessions/src/conversions.rs pause_state_to_rpc)

Confirm pause 'Allow writing outside the workspace?' -> actions accept/deny; the user denies -> pause_confirm(session, false), then session.permission_resolved
The user presses Stop while a pause is open -> the daemon reports Interrupted -> the provider emits session.permission_resolved for that pause before the canceled turn event

FSPEC-017.title: Answer fspec HITL questions from Paseo
FSPEC-017.description: fspec's request-user-input tool (HITL) asks the user structured questions by pausing the session: set_hitl_request + SessionStatus Paused, the same SessionStateChange Paused signal as tool approvals. The questions are read with get_hitl_request (idx 81, Option<HitlRequest { questions: [{ id, header, question, options: [{ label, description }] }] }>) and answered with send_hitl_response (idx 79, HitlResponse { cancelled, answers: [{ id, selected, other }] }). Without wiring, a Paseo agent that asks a question hangs until interrupted.

userStory.role: Paseo user running an fspec agent
userStory.action: answer the questions the agent asks me inside Paseo's question card
userStory.benefit: the agent gets my answer and continues instead of hanging

rules.text: On SessionStateChange Paused the provider checks get_pause_state first and, when it is None, get_hitl_request (idx 81); a HITL request becomes one session.permission { kind: 'question', name: 'question', title: the first question's header, input: { questions } }

Each fspec question maps to a Paseo question { header: the fspec header (or its id when empty), question, options: [{ label, description }], multiSelect: false, allowOther: true, allowEmpty: false } because fspec accepts free text on every question

An allow answer carries updatedInput.answers keyed by header; for each question an answer equal to option labels (comma-separated) becomes selected labels with other null, any other text becomes other with no selected labels, and a question with no answer becomes selected [] / other null; the provider sends send_hitl_response(cancelled false) with one answer per question in fspec order
A deny answer (Paseo Dismiss) sends send_hitl_response with cancelled true and no answers
HITL requests share the approval-pause lifecycle: exactly one session.permission_resolved per request, also when the pause ends another way, and late answers are ignored

examples.text: fspec asks [{id: 'q1', header: 'Env', question: 'Which environment?', options: [dev (local), prod (live)]}]; Paseo shows a question card; the user picks 'dev' -> send_hitl_response(session, { cancelled: false, answers: [{ id: 'q1', selected: ['dev'], other: null }] })
The user types 'staging' instead of choosing an option -> answers: [{ id: 'q1', selected: [], other: 'staging' }]
The user dismisses the card -> send_hitl_response(session, { cancelled: true, answers: [] }) and session.permission_resolved

architectureNotes.text: server/wire.ts: getHitlRequest (81) -> Option<HitlRequest>, sendHitlResponse (79, session_id, HitlResponse) -> Result<(), String>, checked against Rust golden vectors. server/session.ts: openPause falls back to get_hitl_request; the open-pause record gains a 'hitl' kind with its questions; permission() maps Paseo answers to HitlAnswer. Paseo answer format: packages/app/src/components/question-form-card-core.ts buildQuestionFormAnswers (answers[header] = labels joined with ', ' or the custom text). fspec source: rust/agent-loop/src/agent_loop/handlers.rs (set_hitl_request + Paused), rust/rpc-types/src/lib.rs (Hitl* types).

FSPEC-018.title: Answer fspec interactions with the request-bound interaction API
FSPEC-018.description: FSPEC-016/017 answer approval pauses and HITL questions with the legacy calls pause_triple (78), pause_confirm (77) and send_hitl_response (79). fspec documents get_interaction_snapshot (idx 119, -> Result<String JSON, String>) and reply_interaction_checked (idx 120, session_id, method, request_id, arguments JSON) as the 'atomic request-bound replacement for legacy pause/HITL responses' (rust/rpc/src/service_declaration/finish.rs). The legacy calls can answer a pause that was replaced by a newer one. Move approval, HITL and exec-stdin answers onto the snapshot request identities so an answer only applies to the request Paseo showed.

userStory.role: Paseo user approving or answering an fspec agent
userStory.action: have my answer applied only to the exact approval or question Paseo showed me
userStory.benefit: a late or stale click can never approve a different, newer tool call

rules.text: On SessionStateChange Paused the provider reads get_interaction_snapshot (idx 119, Result<String JSON, String>) instead of get_pause_state / get_hitl_request; the JSON is { pause: { request_id, state: { kind, tool_name, message, details } | null }, hitl: { request_id, state: { questions: [{ id, header, question, options: [{label, description}] | null }] } | null } }

Every answer goes through reply_interaction_checked (idx 120: session_id, method, request_id, arguments JSON): Triple -> method pause_triple { choice: Approve | ApproveSession | Deny }; Confirm -> pause_confirm { accept }; Continue -> pause_resume {}; HITL -> send_hitl_response { response: { cancelled, answers: [{ id, selected, other }] } }, always with the request_id from the snapshot the request was built from
The approval request uses the snapshot's separate fields: name = tool_name, description = message (plus details when present), detail = the running tool call's detail
Continue pauses (fspec PauseKind::Continue) show a single Continue action; any answer resumes them with pause_resume
When reply_interaction_checked fails (the daemon's request moved on), the shown request is resolved and the snapshot is read again so the current interaction is shown instead

examples.text: Snapshot pause { request_id: 'p-7', state: { kind: 'Triple', tool_name: 'Bash', message: 'RLCD security: P(risk)=0.46 >= promptThreshold 0.45', details: 'An AI coding agent is about to run ...' } } -> permission name 'Bash'; Approve for session -> reply_interaction_checked(session, 'pause_triple', 'p-7', '{"choice":"ApproveSession"}')

Snapshot hitl { request_id: 'h-2', state: { questions: [{ id: 'q1', header: 'Env', question: 'Which?', options: [dev, prod] }] } } -> question card; answer dev -> reply_interaction_checked(session, 'send_hitl_response', 'h-2', '{"response":{"cancelled":false,"answers":[{"id":"q1","selected":["dev"],"other":null}]}}')
The user approves request p-7 but the daemon already replaced it with p-8: reply returns Err -> permission_resolved for p-7, snapshot read again, new permission for p-8

Live daemon 0.10.9: get_interaction_snapshot on an idle session returns {"pause":{"request_id":"","state":null},"hitl":{"request_id":"","state":null}}; an unknown session returns Err('Session unavailable')

architectureNotes.text: New server/interactions.ts (pure): parse the snapshot JSON, build the Paseo permission request, map a Paseo answer to { method, arguments }. server/session.ts openPause uses getInteractionSnapshot and permission() uses replyInteractionChecked; the legacy get_pause_state/get_hitl_request/pause_*/send_hitl_response calls are no longer used by the session (codec keeps them). Updates FSPEC-016/017 feature steps that named the legacy RPCs. Sources: rust/sessions/src/background_session/interactions.rs interaction_snapshot, rust/sessions/src/handle_impl.rs reply_interaction_checked.

FSPEC-019.title: Surface exec stdin requests so interactive commands do not hang
FSPEC-019.description: fspec's exec tool can wait for typed stdin: the stream carries ExecStdinRequest (StreamChunk 27) and ExecStdinRequestCleared (28); the request is read with get_exec_stdin_request (session) -> Option<ExecStdinRequest> and answered with write_exec_stdin(session, exec_session_id, text) (TOOL-022). The provider drops both chunks, so an agent running an interactive command hangs in Paseo exactly like unwired approvals did. Show it as a Paseo free-text question (or permission) tied to the running tool card and resolve it on ExecStdinRequestCleared.

userStory.role: Paseo user whose fspec agent runs an interactive command
userStory.action: type the input the command is waiting for from Paseo
userStory.benefit: interactive commands finish instead of hanging the agent

rules.text: The codec decodes StreamChunk 27 as execStdinRequest { execSessionId, command, quietSeconds, tsMs } and 28 as execStdinRequestCleared instead of unsupported

A live execStdinRequest becomes one session.permission { kind: 'question', name: 'stdin', title: 'Input for <command>' } with one free-text question (header 'Input', no options, allowOther true, allowEmpty true) explaining the command has been quiet for <quietSeconds>s
An allow answer writes the typed text with write_exec_stdin (idx 83: session_id, exec_session_id, text); fspec appends the trailing newline; a deny answer writes nothing

The request resolves exactly once: after the answer is written, on execStdinRequestCleared, on a newer request for another exec session, on the turn's terminal chunk, on close and on connection loss; replayed history never opens a stdin request
Exec stdin requests are independent of approval pauses: both can be open at once and each resolves on its own

examples.text: Bash runs 'python3 -c "input()"' and goes quiet: chunk ExecStdinRequest { exec_session_id: 'exec-3', command: 'python3 -c input()', quiet_seconds: 5 } -> Paseo shows 'Input for python3 -c input()'; the user types 'hello' -> write_exec_stdin(session, 'exec-3', 'hello') -> session.permission_resolved
The command finishes on its own before the user answers: ExecStdinRequestCleared -> session.permission_resolved, and a late answer writes nothing
The user dismisses the stdin card -> no write_exec_stdin, the request resolves; the agent can still interrupt or wait

Source: rust/rpc-types/src/lib.rs ExecStdinRequest (exec_session_id, command, quiet_seconds, ts_ms); TOOL-022 write_exec_stdin appends a newline.

userStory.action: see each fspec command and its output as a readable card
userStory.benefit: I can follow the agent's spec work without decoding raw JSON, and nothing waits on Paseo

FSPEC-021.title: Show fspec subordinate agents as Paseo child sessions
FSPEC-021.description: fspec agents can spawn subordinate sessions (AgentManager; get_subordinate idx 69, get_subordinates idx 70, supervisors 66-68, receive_incoming_message 71, IncomingMessage chunk 16). The provider only routes stream chunks for daemon sessions it opened, so subordinate work is invisible in Paseo. Paseo supports provider-owned child sessions (session.opened with parentSessionId/toolCallId, restoration 'parent'; capability session.subsession). Map subordinates to child sessions and stream their transcripts.

userStory.role: Paseo user whose fspec agent spawns sub-agents
userStory.action: see each sub-agent as a child session under the agent that spawned it
userStory.benefit: I can follow and steer delegated work instead of it happening invisibly

rules.text: The first stream chunk for a daemon session the provider has not mapped triggers one get_supervisors (idx 66) lookup; when a supervisor is an open Paseo session the provider opens a Paseo child session for it, otherwise the daemon session is remembered as foreign and its chunks are ignored

A child opens with session.opened { sessionId: '<parent>:sub:<daemon id>', parentSessionId: the parent's Paseo id, restoration: 'parent', capabilities, cwd, title: the subordinate's role/name when known, toolCallId: the parent's tool call whose result mentions the subordinate id when there is one } followed by session.config
Chunks that arrive while the supervisor lookup is pending are buffered and published to the child in order once it opens, so no subordinate output is lost

A child is a full registry session bound to the existing subordinate daemon session: prompts, interrupts, permissions and stdin work as for any session, but the provider never creates, resumes or destroys the subordinate itself
When the daemon reports the subordinate removed (SessionEvent removed) or the parent closes, the child is closed with session.closed and its daemon session is left to fspec

examples.text: Parent paseo-1 (daemon fspec-sess-42) calls AgentManager spawn; its ToolResult content mentions 'sub-9'; the first Text chunk for 'sub-9' -> get_supervisors('sub-9') = ['fspec-sess-42'] -> session.opened { sessionId: 'paseo-1:sub:sub-9', parentSessionId: 'paseo-1', restoration: 'parent', toolCallId: the spawn call id }, then the buffered Text is published to the child
A chunk for daemon session 'tui-5' driven by the fspec TUI: get_supervisors('tui-5') = [] -> ignored, and later chunks for 'tui-5' cause no further lookups
The daemon emits SessionEvent removed for 'sub-9' -> session.closed for 'paseo-1:sub:sub-9'; no destroy_session is sent

architectureNotes.text: server/wire.ts: getSupervisors (66) -> Vec<SessionId>. server/session.ts: unknown daemon ids go through a pending-lookup map (buffered chunks) -> openChild or foreign set; children are FspecSession entries with parentSessionId and owned=false so close/closeAll skip destroy_session; handleSessionEvent(removed) closes mapped children. server/provider.ts routes sessionEvent envelopes. server/transcript.ts: toolCallMentioning(text) finds the spawning tool call. Source: rust/agent-loop/src/agent_manager_handler.rs (create_session_with_id then add_supervisor), Paseo plugin-provider.ts acceptProviderChild.

FSPEC-022.title: List and import fspec sessions in Paseo
FSPEC-022.description: Paseo's 'sessions' input (capability session.list) lists provider sessions for import, then opens one with its persistence. fspec exposes list_sessions(project_path) (idx 1, -> Vec<SessionInfo>) and list_live_sessions (idx 2); resume_session (55) and replay (FSPEC-006/009/013) already reopen a session. Wire session.list so past fspec sessions for the daemon's workspace can be browsed and imported.

userStory.role: Paseo user with past fspec sessions
userStory.action: browse and import fspec sessions from Paseo's session list
userStory.benefit: work started in the fspec TUI or an earlier Paseo agent can be continued in Paseo

rules.text: The provider advertises 'session.list' and answers a 'sessions' input with exactly one 'sessions' event for its requestId, built from list_sessions (idx 1) for the daemon's workspace (get_workspace_info)

Each fspec session becomes { persistence: { version: 1, data: { sessionId } }, cwd: the daemon workspace, title: the session name, description: '<n> messages' plus the model when known, updatedAt: ISO time of updated_at_ms when present }, newest first
Sessions already open on this connection are left out; a query keeps sessions whose name or id contains it (case-insensitive); limit caps the count
A cwd outside the daemon's workspace yields an empty list, because that daemon cannot open sessions there (FSPEC-015)
Importing a listed session is a normal session.open with that persistence, which resumes it (FSPEC-009) and can replay its history (FSPEC-006/013)

Query 'login' -> only 'Fix login'; limit 1 -> only the newest

FSPEC-023.title: Offer fspec session commands in the Paseo composer
FSPEC-023.description: Paseo publishes provider commands with session.commands and sends them as prompts with input.type 'command' (capability prompt.command), answered with prompt_result completed when no turn runs. fspec offers compact_session (idx 52, -> CompactionResult), clear_history (51), set_continue_state (40, enabled + budget), set_goal_state (42, goal + success criteria) and their getters (41, 43). Expose /compact, /clear, /continue and /goal, and render their results (compaction row, notices). Include /focus <work-unit-id|none> via set_work_unit_focus (idx 57: session, work_unit_id Option<String>, source) so Paseo users can tell the agent which story it is working on; the agent then attributes tool calls (required work_unit_id) to it instead of NONE.

userStory.role: Paseo user driving an fspec agent
userStory.action: use fspec's session commands (/compact, /clear, /continue, /goal, /focus) from Paseo's composer
userStory.benefit: I can manage context, autonomy, goals and the work unit without switching to the fspec TUI

rules.text: The provider advertises 'prompt.command' and publishes session.commands right after session.config on every open: compact, clear, continue [on|off|N], goal [text|clear|verify <cmd>], focus <work-unit-id|none>
A command prompt runs without starting a turn and is answered with exactly one session.prompt_result: completed (plus an info session.notice describing the outcome) or failed with the reason
compact calls compact_session (idx 52) and reports original -> compacted tokens; clear calls clear_history (51)

continue mirrors the fspec TUI: no argument toggles (turning on uses budget 10), on = budget 10, off disables, N > 0 sets the budget and enables, 0 or other text is rejected, and off is refused while a goal is active; it reads get_continue_state (41) / get_goal_state (43) and writes set_continue_state (40)

An unknown command name is answered with prompt_result failed 'Unknown fspec command /<name>'
