/continue 25 -> set_continue_state(session, true, 25); /continue off while goal 'ship' is active -> prompt_result failed 'auto-continue: a goal is active — clear the goal first (/goal clear)'
/goal ship -> set_goal_state(session, Some(('ship', None))); then /goal verify npm test -> set_goal_state(session, Some(('ship', Some('npm test'))))
/focus FSPEC-001 -> set_work_unit_focus(session, Some('FSPEC-001'), 'paseo'); /focus none -> set_work_unit_focus(session, None, 'paseo')

userStory.action: revert the working tree to an fspec checkpoint from the timeline

FSPEC-025.description: The daemon streams WorkUnitsUpdate (chunk 22 and Envelope::WorkUnitsUpdate), work-unit focus (SessionEvent FocusChanged; get/set_work_unit_focus 56-57) and continue/goal state (chunk 26). userStory.action: see which work unit the agent is focused on and which work unit each tool call is charged to
userStory.benefit: I can follow the agent's progress against the fspec board from Paseo

Each Paseo session shows one 'todo' timeline item (id '<epoch>:focus') for its focused work unit: one entry '<id> — <title>' with status in_progress, or completed when the work unit status is done; it is seeded after the open from get_work_unit_focus (idx 56) only when a work unit is focused, and re-published on every SessionEvent focusChanged for that session, where a cleared focus shows the entry 'No work unit in focus' as pending

examples.text: Open: get_work_unit_focus = { context: { id: 'BUG-285', title: 'sync-version flag', status: 'backlog' } } -> todo item [{ text: 'BUG-285 — sync-version flag', status: 'in_progress', completed: false }]

/focus FSPEC-001 -> SessionEvent focusChanged { context: { id: 'FSPEC-001', title: 'Scaffold', status: 'done' } } -> the same todo id re-published with [{ text: 'FSPEC-001 — Scaffold', status: 'completed', completed: true }]

Bash tool call with input { command: 'ls', work_unit_id: 'FSPEC-001' } -> tool_call metadata { workUnitId: 'FSPEC-001' }; fspec tool call with { command: 'show-work-unit', work_unit_id: 'FSPEC-001' } -> label 'fspec show-work-unit · FSPEC-001'

architectureNotes.text: server/wire.ts: getWorkUnitFocus (56, Result<WorkUnitFocus, String>). server/session.ts: publishFocus(session, focus) on open and on sessionEvent focusChanged. server/transcript.ts: toolItem adds metadata.workUnitId and the fspec label suffix. WorkUnitFocus/WorkUnitContext are already decoded by the FSPEC-002 codec.

FSPEC-026.title: Send images from Paseo prompts to fspec
FSPEC-026.description: Paseo prompts can carry image content (capability prompt.image); the provider only sends text via send_input. fspec has image input on supervisor messages (receive_incoming_message, IncomingMessageInput with images; IncomingMessage chunk 16 has images). Research whether a session prompt can carry images over RPC; if so, advertise prompt.image and send them, otherwise document the limitation.

userStory.role: Paseo user prompting an fspec agent
userStory.action: attach images and files to my prompt
userStory.benefit: the agent can look at screenshots and files I share instead of the attachment being dropped

questions.text: @human: fspec has no image input for a user prompt (send_input is text-only; receive_incoming_message frames images as a supervisor message). How should Paseo images reach the agent?
questions.answer: User chose: write each image to a private temp folder outside the repo and append '[Attached image: <path>]' to the prompt so the agent opens it with its Read tool; uploaded files are referenced by their path.

rules.text: User chose: write each image to a private temp folder outside the repo and append '[Attached image: <path>]' to the prompt so the agent opens it with its Read tool; uploaded files are referenced by their path.

The provider advertises 'prompt.image'; each image part is decoded from base64 and written to <os tmp>/fspec-paseo/<session>/image-<n>.<ext> (directory mode 0700, extension from the MIME type), and the prompt text gains one line '[Attached image: <path>]' per image after the typed text
An uploaded_file part adds '[Attached file: <path>]' using the path Paseo already stored; text parts and text attachments stay in the prompt text as before
A session's temp image folder is removed when the session closes or the connection closes

examples.text: Prompt 'what is wrong here?' + one PNG -> send_input(session, 'what is wrong here?\n\n[Attached image: /tmp/fspec-paseo/paseo-1/image-1.png]') and that file holds the decoded PNG bytes
Prompt 'review this' + uploaded_file { path: '/Users/me/.paseo/uploads/spec.pdf' } -> '... [Attached file: /Users/me/.paseo/uploads/spec.pdf]'
Session paseo-1 closes -> /tmp/fspec-paseo/paseo-1 is deleted

architectureNotes.text: New server/attachments.ts: writes image parts and formats attachment lines; session.ts prompt() builds text through it and removes the folder on close/closeAll; provider.ts advertises prompt.image. fspec's Read tool reads images (BUG-138). No RPC change.

FSPEC-027.title: Answer Paseo idle-runtime checks for fspec sessions
FSPEC-027.description: Paseo asks session.can_stop_runtime before releasing an idle runtime (must never be answered with request.completed). fspec exposes get_session_status (6), pending input (get_pending_input 60), exec stdin requests and subordinates, which tell whether stopping would lose work. Implement can_stop_runtime (capability session.can_stop_runtime) so Paseo can release idle fspec sessions safely.

userStory.role: Paseo user with idle fspec agents
userStory.action: let Paseo release idle fspec runtimes only when nothing would be lost
userStory.benefit: resources are freed without killing background work or pending questions

rules.text: The provider advertises 'session.can_stop_runtime' and answers each such input with exactly one session.can_stop_runtime event (never request.completed) carrying canStop

canStop is true only when the session has no queued or running turn, no open approval/HITL request, no open stdin request, no open sub-agent child, the daemon reports get_session_status (idx 6) idle, and get_pending_input (idx 60) is empty
The check never changes the session; an RPC failure answers canStop false so the runtime stays alive

examples.text: Idle session, status idle, no pending input -> canStop true
A turn is running (or a sub-agent child is open, or an approval prompt is pending) -> canStop false without asking the daemon
get_session_status fails -> canStop false

architectureNotes.text: server/wire.ts: getPendingInput (60, Option<String>); getSessionStatus (6) already in the codec. server/session.ts canStopRuntime(input). Releasing an idle runtime closes the session (destroy_session), and a later reopen resumes it (FSPEC-009).

FSPEC-028.title: Strip fspec stderr markers from shell output
FSPEC-028.description: fspec's ToolResult content marks stderr lines with a '⚠stderr⚠' prefix (seen live: '⚠stderr⚠real\t0m0.017s\n⚠stderr⚠user ...'), while ToolProgress carries is_stderr separately. The provider shows the markers verbatim in Paseo shell cards. Strip the markers from result content (keeping the text) so completed shell output reads cleanly.

userStory.role: Paseo user reading an fspec agent's shell output
userStory.action: see command output without fspec's internal stderr markers
userStory.benefit: completed shell cards read like real terminal output

rules.text: fspec prefixes each stderr line of a ToolResult with the marker '⚠stderr⚠'; the provider removes every marker from tool output (results and progress) and keeps the text
Output without markers is unchanged, and the same cleaning applies to live and replayed transcripts

examples.text:
Live: ToolResult content '⚠stderr⚠real	0m0.017s
⚠stderr⚠user	0m0.004s
' -> shell card output 'real	0m0.017s
user	0m0.004s
'

architectureNotes.text: server/transcript.ts: strip the marker where tool output is stored (toolResult content and toolProgress chunks) so every rendering (shell, fspec, unknown) is clean.

FSPEC-029.title: Keep Paseo agents and fspec agent tabs in sync
FSPEC-029.description: Paseo agents and fspec's live agent tabs should mirror each other. Today: opening a Paseo agent creates/resumes a live fspec session and closing destroys it, but (1) the plugin never calls set_active_session (idx 62), which the fspec TUI calls on create/attach/cycle (rust/fspec-tui/src/app/session_restore.rs spawn_set_active_session) and which drives the board's live indicator (green dot); and (2) when a session is closed on the fspec side (SessionEvent Removed / Cleared on the stream) the matching Paseo agent stays open as a dead tab. Set the active session on open/prompt and clear it (clear_active_session idx 63, guarded by get_active_session idx 64 so another client's choice is not clobbered) on close, connection close and daemon drop; close the Paseo session (session.closed) when fspec removes its daemon session. Top-level sessions started in fspec are surfaced through import (FSPEC-022) and spawned subordinates as child sessions (FSPEC-021), since a Paseo provider cannot open top-level tabs on its own.

userStory.role: user running fspec agents from Paseo and the fspec TUI
userStory.action: see the same agents open on both sides
userStory.benefit: the fspec board shows the Paseo agent as live and closing on either side closes it on the other

rules.text: When a Paseo session opens (new or resumed) the provider calls set_active_session (idx 62) with its daemon session, and again whenever that session is prompted, so fspec's board shows the session Paseo is driving as live, like the fspec TUI does on create/attach/cycle

Closing an owned Paseo session needs no extra call: destroy_session already clears fspec's active pointer when it pointed at that session (fspec BUG-206); closing a sub-agent child calls clear_active_session (idx 63) only when get_active_session (idx 64) still names that child's daemon session, so another client's choice is never clobbered
When fspec removes a daemon session that backs an open Paseo session (SessionEvent removed), the Paseo session closes with session.closed, its open requests resolve, and no destroy_session is sent
A failing active-session call never fails the open, prompt or close it accompanies

examples.text: Paseo opens paseo-1 -> create_session = fspec-sess-42 -> set_active_session(fspec-sess-42); the fspec board shows that agent as live
The user closes the agent tab in the fspec TUI -> SessionEvent removed for fspec-sess-42 -> Paseo gets session.closed for paseo-1
Two Paseo agents are open; the user prompts the second -> set_active_session(its daemon id), so the board follows the agent being driven

architectureNotes.text: server/wire.ts: setActiveSession (62, unit), clearActiveSession (63, unit), getActiveSession (64, Option<SessionId>). server/session.ts: open() and prompt() call markActive(session) (errors swallowed); handleSessionEvent(removed) closes owned sessions too; closeChild clears the pointer when it names the child. fspec source: rust/fspec-tui/src/app/session_restore.rs spawn_set_active_session; rust/sessions/src/session_manager.rs destroy_session clears active_session_id (BUG-206).

FSPEC-030.title: Show idle fspec sub-agents as finished in Paseo
FSPEC-030.description: Paseo opens every provider child as running and only moves it on session.turn. Sub-agent work is driven by its supervisor (AgentManager), not a Paseo prompt, so no turn is ever started and the daemon's done chunk is dropped by settle(): the child shows running forever after the sub-agent goes idle.

userStory.role: Paseo user whose fspec agent spawns sub-agents
userStory.action: see each sub-agent's child session go idle when it finishes its work
userStory.benefit: I can tell which delegated work is still running

rules.text: Paseo shows a provider child as running until it receives a session.turn terminal for it, so a sub-agent's own runs must be reported as provider turns

When a child session has no started or queued turn and receives a work chunk (responseAttemptStarted, text, thinking, toolCall, toolResult, toolProgress, userInput, providerWaiting, or sessionStateChange running), the provider starts a turn for it (session.turn started, turnId turn-N) before publishing the chunk
The daemon's done/error/interrupted chunk settles that turn completed/failed/canceled exactly as for a prompted turn, so the child shows idle (completed) once the sub-agent stops

Chunks that are not work (tokenUpdate, contextFillUpdate, userNotification, sessionStateChange idle, ...) never start a turn, and owned (non-child) sessions keep starting turns only from Paseo prompts
A Paseo prompt sent to a child while a supervisor-driven turn runs is queued behind it, as the daemon queues the input

examples.text: Child paseo-1:sub:sub-9 is adopted from a Text chunk 'working' -> session.opened, session.turn started turn-1, the assistant text, then a done chunk -> session.turn completed turn-1
The supervisor messages idle sub-9 again: a userInput chunk starts turn-2 and the next done completes it
A tokenUpdate chunk for idle child sub-9 starts no turn
A Text chunk for owned session paseo-1 with no prompt starts no turn

architectureNotes.text: Paseo plugin-provider.ts attachChild upserts provider_subagent status running; acceptChildEvent maps only session.turn (started->running, else the state) and session.closed/runtime_failed to a status. server/session.ts handleChunk: for !session.owned, start a turn via the existing queue/advance path when activeTurnId is null and the queue is empty and the chunk is work.

FSPEC-031.title: Close fspec sub-agent sessions when their Paseo parent closes
FSPEC-031.description: Closing a parent Paseo session sends destroy_session for the parent only. fspec's destroy_session does not cascade (it only unlinks the chain of command), so subordinates keep running as orphans. The provider must list subordinates (get_subordinates idx 70) before destroying the parent, since destroy unlinks them, and destroy them too.

userStory.role: Paseo user whose fspec agent spawns sub-agents
userStory.action: have closing the agent also close the sub-agents it spawned
userStory.benefit: no orphaned fspec sessions keep running after I close the agent

questions.text: @human: How deep should closing a parent close its sub-agents?
questions.answer: The whole tree: sub-agents of sub-agents too

questions.text: @human: What happens to a sub-agent also supervised by a session outside the closing tree?
questions.answer: Leave it running; only its Paseo child view closes

questions.text: @human: Should provider shutdown (closeAll) also destroy sub-agents?
questions.answer: Yes, the same cleanup as closing each parent

rules.text: Before destroying an owned session the provider lists its subordinates with get_subordinates (idx 70), recursively, because fspec's destroy_session does not cascade and unlinks the chain of command

A sub-agent is destroyed only when every one of its supervisors (get_supervisors idx 66) is the closing session or a sub-agent being destroyed; a sub-agent with any other supervisor is left running and its own sub-agents are not visited
Sub-agents are destroyed deepest first, then the parent; a failed lookup or sub-agent destroy never stops the parent being destroyed and closed
The Paseo child sessions of the closing parent still close with session.closed, as before
closeAll (provider shutdown) applies the same sub-agent cleanup to every owned session

examples.text: Paseo closes paseo-1 (daemon fspec-sess-42) whose sub-agent sub-9 has sub-agent sub-10: destroy_session sub-10, then sub-9, then fspec-sess-42; child paseo-1:sub:sub-9 closes
Sub-agent sub-9 is also supervised by TUI session tui-5: closing paseo-1 destroys only fspec-sess-42; sub-9 keeps running
destroy_session for sub-9 fails: fspec-sess-42 is still destroyed and paseo-1 closes
Provider shutdown with paseo-1 open destroys sub-9 and fspec-sess-42

architectureNotes.text: server/wire.ts: add getSubordinates (66 sibling, idx 70) -> Vec<SessionId>, same shape as getSupervisors. server/session.ts: a destroyTree(daemonSessionId) helper used by close() and closeAll(). Supersedes FSPEC-021 rule 4's 'its daemon session is left to fspec' for the parent-close case; a removed sub-agent (SessionEvent removed) is still never destroyed.

FSPEC-032.title: Find fspec sessions in Paseo's import list by their conversation text
FSPEC-032.description: Paseo's Import session search only matches fspec sessions by name and id (server/session.ts list()), so a query like 'VTCode' that appears in a recent session's messages finds nothing; only other providers' (e.g. Copilot) sessions show. Investigate persistence_search_history (idx 26) to match message content.

userStory.role: Paseo user importing fspec sessions
userStory.action: find a past fspec session by searching for something I said in it
userStory.benefit: I can resume the right session without remembering its name

rules.text: With a non-empty query the provider calls persistence_search_history (idx 26) for the workspace and lists every persisted session whose id appears in a match, as well as sessions whose name or id contains the query

Paseo re-filters provider results on title, prompt previews and cwd basename, so a session found by prompt text carries its most recent matching prompt (trimmed, at most 200 characters) as its description
Only sessions listSessions returns for the workspace (and not already open) are listed; matches for other session ids are ignored
If persistence_search_history fails the list falls back to name/id matching; an empty query lists as before

assumptions: fspec's history search covers the prompts the user typed, not agent replies; searching replies would mean paging every transcript and is out of scope

examples.text: Session 'Refactor terminal' (sess-7) had the prompt 'port the VTCode diff view'; searching 'vtcode' lists sess-7 with description 'port the VTCode diff view'
Searching 'refactor' still lists sess-7 by its name with the usual '<n> messages' description
persistence_search_history returns an error: searching 'refactor' still lists sess-7 by name
A history match for a deleted session sess-99 that listSessions no longer returns is not listed

architectureNotes.text: server/wire.ts: persistenceSearchHistory (26) { query: String } -> Result<Vec<HistoryMatch { session_id, text, timestamp_iso }>, String>. server/session.ts list(). Paseo agent-manager.ts matchesImportableSessionQuery filters on title/firstPromptPreview/lastPromptPreview/cwd basename; plugin-provider.ts maps description -> lastPromptPreview.

FSPEC-033.title: Answer fspec sub-agent approvals and questions from the parent agent in Paseo
FSPEC-033.description: Paseo drops session.permission/permission_resolved events from provider child sessions (plugin-provider.ts acceptChildEvent keeps only timeline items, turns and closes), so a sub-agent's approval pause, HITL question or stdin request never shows anywhere and the sub-agent hangs. Route them to the root Paseo session and route the answer back to the sub-agent.

userStory.role: Paseo user whose fspec agent spawns sub-agents
userStory.action: approve and answer every sub-agent's approvals, questions and input prompts from the parent agent's thread
userStory.benefit: sub-agents never hang waiting on a prompt I cannot see

rules.text: Paseo only shows permissions raised on a root session; a child's session.permission is dropped, so every sub-agent pause (approval or HITL) and stdin request is emitted on its top-level Paseo ancestor
A sub-agent's request title is prefixed with the sub-agent's label (e.g. 'Sub-agent sub-9: Allow Bash?') so the user knows who is asking; the parent's own requests are unchanged

Paseo answers on the root session; the provider routes the answer by permission id to the sub-agent that raised it and replies to that sub-agent's daemon session (reply_interaction_checked or write_exec_stdin)
session.permission_resolved for a sub-agent's request is also emitted on the root, however it ends (answered, sub-agent resumed, sub-agent closed)
Nested sub-agents route to the top-level owned session, not their direct parent

examples.text: Sub-agent sub-9 under paseo-1 pauses for Bash approval -> session.permission on paseo-1 titled 'Sub-agent sub-9: Allow Bash?'; the user allows it on paseo-1 -> reply_interaction_checked for daemon session sub-9
Sub-agent sub-9 asks a HITL question 'Which branch?' -> it shows on paseo-1; the user answers 'main' -> the answer goes to sub-9
Sub-agent sub-9's paused state clears (it resumed) -> session.permission_resolved on paseo-1
sub-10 (sub-agent of sub-9, under paseo-1) pauses -> the request shows on paseo-1

architectureNotes.text: Paseo plugin-provider.ts: acceptChildEvent handles only timeline.item, session.turn, session.closed/runtime_failed; translatePermission/respondToPermission are root-session only. server/session.ts: openPause, openStdin, resolvePause, resolveStdin emit on rootOf(session); permission() finds the session (root or descendant) whose pause/stdin permissionId matches.

FSPEC-034.title: Serve the live fspec board to Paseo plugin UI
FSPEC-034.description: Plugin-server board store fed by the shared daemon socket (Envelope::WorkUnitsUpdate, SessionSnapshot, SessionEvent focusChanged), with a revision counter and a long-poll plugin RPC (fspec.board.watch, held <=20s because Paseo's plugin-process request timeout is 30s) so the UI gets near-realtime updates without server->UI push. Applies the FSPEC-015 workspace guard.

userStory.role: Paseo user running fspec on desktop or mobile
userStory.action: have the plugin server keep the fspec board live and hand it to the board panel
userStory.benefit: the panel shows the same board the fspec TUI shows, within about a second of every change, without polling the daemon

rules.text: Which fspec sessions are focused on which work unit comes from SessionInfo.workUnitFocus in the seed and from SessionEvent focusChanged; a cleared focus removes the session from its work unit

Every observable change (new units snapshot that differs, focus change, connection lost, reconnected) gets a new opaque revision string '<instance epoch>:<counter>' so a restarted plugin server never reuses a revision a panel already holds

Plugin RPC fspec.board.watch({ cwd, sinceRevision }) answers immediately when sinceRevision is null or differs from the current revision; otherwise it holds until the next change or 20 seconds (Paseo's plugin-process request timeout is 30 s), then answers with the current board
The board is only served for a cwd inside the daemon's workspace (FSPEC-015 guard); otherwise watch answers state 'unavailable' with the same 'the fspec daemon serves X, not Y' reason
When the daemon is unreachable or the connection drops, watch answers state 'unavailable' with the reason (held waiters are woken); the next watch call reconnects and re-seeds
The plugin server opens one board daemon connection lazily on the first watch and closes it, waking every held watch, when the plugin is unloaded

The board comes from the daemon over its own socket, never from reading spec files: seeded from the connect-time WorkUnitsUpdate and SessionSnapshot frames (which arrive before connect() resolves, so the daemon client keeps them as connection.initial), then kept current by every Envelope::WorkUnitsUpdate (full snapshot replace, daemon column order preserved)

list_live_sessions (idx 2) answers Vec<SessionId> (bare ids), not Vec<SessionInfo>; the codec must decode it as strings or the response frame is dropped and the request hangs (found against the real daemon during FSPEC-034)

examples.text: First watch { cwd: '/ws', sinceRevision: null } with the daemon serving /ws and list_work_units = [FSPEC-001 backlog 3pts] -> { state: 'ready', revision: 'E:1', workspace: '/ws', units: [FSPEC-001 ...], focus: {} }

Panel holds watch { sinceRevision: 'E:1' }; the daemon pushes WorkUnitsUpdate moving FSPEC-001 to specifying -> the held watch answers within the push with revision 'E:2' and FSPEC-001 status specifying
Held watch { sinceRevision: 'E:2' } with no change for 20 s -> answers { state: 'ready', revision: 'E:2' } with the unchanged board
watch { cwd: '/elsewhere' } while the daemon serves /ws -> { state: 'unavailable', reason: 'the fspec daemon serves /ws, not /elsewhere — start fspec in /elsewhere to use it there' }

Held watch, then the daemon socket closes -> the watch answers { state: 'unavailable', reason: 'fspec daemon connection was lost: ...' }; the next watch reconnects and answers 'ready' with a fresh seed

Connect-time SessionSnapshot has fspec-sess-1 focused on FSPEC-001; then focusChanged moves fspec-sess-1 to FSPEC-002 -> focus goes from { 'FSPEC-001': ['fspec-sess-1'] } to { 'FSPEC-002': ['fspec-sess-1'] } with a new revision
list_live_sessions response bytes [len=2]['fspec-sess-1','fspec-sess-2'] decode to { sessionIds: ['fspec-sess-1','fspec-sess-2'] }

architectureNotes.text: New: shared/board.ts (defineRpc contract + zod schemas, imported by server and later the client), server/board.ts (board store + watch handler built on createFspecDaemonClient; reuses within() from server/session.ts), index.server.ts registers server.handle(watchBoardRpc, ...) and disposes the store in its cleanup. The board uses its own daemon client (own socket) like each provider connection does.

assumptions: Column grouping, points summary and display limits are the panel's job (FSPEC-035); the store returns the daemon's flat, ordered WorkUnitInfo list

FSPEC-035.title: Show the fspec board as a native Paseo workspace panel
FSPEC-035.description: index.client.tsx registers a workspace panel (plus Command Center item and /board slash command) rendering the seven fspec columns with TUI card labels (ID [pts], green dot for focused cards, latest-change marker), points summary and search. Wide layouts show side-by-side columns; compact (mobile) layouts show a column picker with counts and one vertical list.

userStory.role: Paseo user on desktop or mobile
userStory.action: open an fspec board panel in a workspace
userStory.benefit: I see the same live Kanban board as the fspec TUI without leaving Paseo

rules.text: The client registers workspace panel 'fspec-board' (title 'fspec board', locations ['workspace']), a workspace Command Center item 'Open fspec board' and a workspace slash command /board, both of which open the panel

The panel long-polls fspec.board.watch with cwd = the workspace directory, re-issuing it as soon as each answer arrives with sinceRevision = the answered revision; a failed RPC is retried after 3 seconds
Columns are the seven fspec states in fixed order backlog, specifying, testing, implementing, validating, done, blocked, each with its card count; cards keep the daemon's order within a column

A card reads like the TUI cell: 'ID [pts]' (points only when estimated) over its title; it is prefixed with a green dot when an fspec session is focused on it, and the single card with the latest lastStateChangeAt is marked as the most recent change
The board footer shows the fspec board summary 'N points in progress, M points completed' (done estimates are completed, every other column is in progress)

Search mirrors the TUI '/' dialog: case-insensitive substring over id (default), title or description (units without a description never match in description mode); choosing a result selects that card and, on compact layouts, switches to its column

Wide layouts show all columns side by side (horizontal scroll), each column a virtualized list; compact layouts (layout.compact, i.e. mobile) show a row of column chips with counts and one virtualized list for the chosen column
The chosen compact column and the selected card persist per panel tab (useTabState)
An unavailable board shows its reason in place of the columns and recovers automatically when the board becomes ready
Compact layouts open on the first non-empty column in board order until the user picks one

questions.text: @human: Cap the done column (1,645 units in fspec) like the CLI's 25 per column, or let it scroll?
questions.answer: Let it scroll: columns are virtualized lists, so no cap is needed (default chosen while moving through the cards; user can overrule)

questions.text: @human: Which column does mobile open on?
questions.answer: The first non-empty column in board order (default chosen; user can overrule)

questions.text: @human: Should the panel also be offered in the desktop explorer sidebar?
questions.answer: No, workspace tab only: seven columns do not fit the narrow explorer (default chosen; user can overrule)

examples.text: Board [FSPEC-001 backlog 3pts, FSPEC-002 done 5pts, FSPEC-003 backlog] -> backlog (2): FSPEC-001 [3], FSPEC-003; done (1): FSPEC-002 [5]; other columns (0); summary '3 points in progress, 5 points completed'
focus { FSPEC-001: ['fspec-sess-1'] } -> FSPEC-001's card label is '🟢 FSPEC-001 [3]'
FSPEC-001 lastStateChangeAt 2026-10-30T01:00Z, FSPEC-002 2026-10-30T02:00Z, FSPEC-003 null -> only FSPEC-002 is marked most recent
Search mode title, query 'SCAFF' -> matches FSPEC-001 'Scaffold the plugin'; mode description with query '' -> only units with a description
Compact layout with backlog empty and specifying holding FSPEC-004 -> opens on specifying; choosing search result FSPEC-002 (done) switches the list to done and selects it
watch answers unavailable 'the fspec daemon serves /ws, not /other — ...' -> the panel shows that text; the next ready answer shows the columns

architectureNotes.text: index.client.tsx (registration), client/board-model.ts (pure: columns, card label, latest marker, summary, search, default compact column — unit tested with vitest), client/use-board.ts (long-poll hook on useRpc + useWorkspace), client/board-panel.tsx (React Native view: wide columns vs compact chips, theme colors only). package.json files + devDeps react 19.2.3, react-native 0.86.3, @types/react, @tanstack/react-query; tsconfig jsx react-jsx; manifest requirements paseo >=0.13.0 (useTabState, unified panel props).

FSPEC-036.title: Show full fspec work unit details from the Paseo board
FSPEC-036.description: Selecting a card shows the TUI details strip (title, description, attachments, epic/estimate/status); 'Show full details' calls get_work_unit_details (RPC idx 123, new at fspec 9fa9a798, not yet in wire.ts) and renders the TUI document sections. Side pane on wide layouts, bottom-sheet Modal on mobile.

userStory.role: Paseo user browsing the fspec board
userStory.action: see a selected card's details and open its full fspec record
userStory.benefit: I can read a work unit's story, rules, examples, questions and relationships from Paseo like in the fspec TUI

rules.text: Selecting a card shows the TUI details strip for it: title, description (or 'No description'), attachments count, and 'Epic | Estimate | Status' from the board snapshot, without an RPC

'Show full details' calls plugin RPC fspec.board.details({ cwd, id }), which calls get_work_unit_details (idx 123, Result<String,String>) on the board's daemon connection, applies the workspace guard and answers { state: 'ready', id, workUnit } from the JSON envelope or { state: 'unavailable', reason }

The full details render the TUI document projection: sections Overview (type, status, epic, estimate), Description, Example Mapping (userStory, rules, examples, questions, assumptions, architectureNotes), Event Storm, Relationships (parent, children, dependsOn, blocks, blockedBy, relatesTo), Attachments, History (stateHistory, statusHistory, blockedReason), Accounting (iterations, actualTokens), Timestamps (createdAt, updatedAt, updated), then Additional Fields for anything else; empty sections are omitted; keys are humanized (dependsOn -> Depends On)
List entries with text read '• text', answered questions add ' → Answer: answer', deleted items add ' [deleted — historical]'; empty arrays read '(none)'
Relationship ids are links: choosing one loads that work unit's full details in the same dialog
Full details open in the host Modal: a bottom sheet on compact (mobile) layouts and a centered dialog on wide layouts

questions.text: @human: Should attachments open from the details?
questions.answer: No: Paseo gives workspace panels no API to open a workspace file, and attachment viewing is the TUI's separate 'a' viewer, not part of the board; attachment paths are shown as selectable text (default chosen; user can overrule)

examples.text: Select FSPEC-001 (epic provider-plugin, 3 pts, backlog, 1 attachment) -> strip 'FSPEC-001 — Scaffold', description, 'Attachments: 1', 'Epic: provider-plugin | Estimate: 3 | Status: backlog'

Record { id, title, type: 'story', status: 'done', rules: [{ id: 0, text: 'R1', deleted: false }, { id: 1, text: 'R0', deleted: true }], questions: [{ text: 'Q?', answer: 'Yes', selected: true }], dependsOn: ['FSPEC-001'], nextRuleId: 2 } -> Overview (Type: story, Status: done), Example Mapping (Rules: • R1 … / • R0 [deleted — historical]; Questions: • Q? → Answer: Yes), Relationships (Depends On: link FSPEC-001), Additional Fields (Next Rule Id: 2)
fspec.board.details({ cwd: '/ws', id: 'NOPE-1' }) with the daemon answering Err('work unit NOPE-1 not found') -> { state: 'unavailable', reason: 'work unit NOPE-1 not found' }

architectureNotes.text: server/wire.ts: getWorkUnitDetails 123 (request id: String; response Result<String, String>). shared/board.ts: detailsBoardRpc. server/board.ts: feed.details(). client/details-model.ts: projectDetails(record) port of fspec-tui components/board_card/{document,document_storm,labels}.rs. client/board-panel.tsx: details strip + Modal with the projected document.

FSPEC-037.title: Reorder fspec cards and open them in an agent from the Paseo board
FSPEC-037.description: Board actions matching the TUI: move a card up/down within its column (move_work_unit_up/down, RPC idx 18/19; not allowed in done) and 'Open in agent' (switch to the Paseo agent whose fspec session is focused on the card, else create an fspec agent focused on it).

userStory.role: Paseo user working an fspec board
userStory.action: reorder cards within a column and open a card in an fspec agent
userStory.benefit: I can prioritise and start work from the Paseo board like I do from the fspec TUI

rules.text: Move up/move down are plugin RPC fspec.board.move({ cwd, id, direction }) calling move_work_unit_up / move_work_unit_down (idx 18/19, Result<(), String>) behind the workspace guard; the answer is { ok: true } or { ok: false, error } and the new order arrives through the normal WorkUnitsUpdate push
The details strip offers Move up and Move down for the selected card except in the done column (the daemon refuses done); a failed move shows its error as a toast

Open in agent switches to the Paseo agent whose fspec session is focused on the card: an agent with provider 'fspec', not closed, whose persistence.metadata.pluginProviderPersistence.data.sessionId is one of the board's focus session ids for that card

When no agent is focused on the card, Open in agent creates an fspec agent in the workspace with model 'fspec/<default model>' (the isDefault model from Paseo's fspec catalog, else the first), title '<id> — <title>' and the initial prompt '/focus <id>' (the provider's focus command, no model turn), then opens it
Open in agent is only offered when the host provides navigation (navigation.openAgent)

examples.text: fspec.board.move({ cwd: '/ws', id: 'FSPEC-003', direction: 'up' }) -> move_work_unit_up('FSPEC-003') -> { ok: true }; daemon Err('cannot move done work unit') -> { ok: false, error: 'cannot move done work unit' }
focus { FSPEC-001: ['fspec-sess-1'] } and agent A1 (fspec, idle, persistence data sessionId fspec-sess-1) -> Open in agent opens A1 without creating anything
FSPEC-002 unfocused, fspec models [m1, m2 (isDefault)] -> creates agent { provider: 'fspec/m2', title: 'FSPEC-002 — Wire codec', prompt: '/focus FSPEC-002' } and opens it

architectureNotes.text: server/wire.ts: moveWorkUnitUp 18, moveWorkUnitDown 19 (request id: String; Result<(), String>). shared/board.ts: moveBoardRpc. server/board.ts: feed.move(). client/open-in-agent.ts: pure focusedAgent()/defaultModel() + openInAgent(deps) with injected Paseo calls. client/board-panel.tsx: strip actions.

FSPEC-038.title: Hold refused fspec board watches instead of answering at once
FSPEC-038.description: Found while building FSPEC-035: fspec.board.watch answers the workspace-guard refusal immediately even when the panel already holds that revision, so a board panel opened in a workspace the daemon does not serve re-polls in a tight loop. The refusal must be held like any other unchanged watch.

userStory.role: Paseo user who opens the fspec board in a workspace the daemon does not serve
userStory.action: see the refusal without the panel hammering the plugin server
userStory.benefit: Paseo and the fspec daemon are not loaded by a tight re-poll loop

rules.text: A watch refused by the workspace guard is held like any other watch when sinceRevision equals the current revision; it answers on the next board change or after the 20 s hold

examples.text: watch { cwd: '/elsewhere', sinceRevision: null } -> refused at once with revision E:1; watch { cwd: '/elsewhere', sinceRevision: 'E:1' } -> held until a WorkUnitsUpdate bumps the revision, then refused again

FSPEC-039.title: Report why fspec could not create a session instead of 'Session not found'
FSPEC-039.description: Paseo's daemon log showed repeated 'Failed to list features for fspec: fspec daemon set_session_model failed: Session not found: ' from the new-agent screen (Paseo opens a throwaway provider session to list a draft's features). Root cause: the provider creates daemon sessions with the legacy create_session (idx 3), which on failure logs the cause in the daemon and returns an empty SessionId (sessions/src/handle_impl.rs:117-121); the provider then calls set_session_model("") and reports a misleading 'Session not found'. fspec offers create_session_checked (idx 121, Result<SessionId, String>) with the real cause.

userStory.role: Paseo user starting an fspec agent
userStory.action: see why fspec could not start a session
userStory.benefit: I can fix the real problem (model backend, credentials) instead of chasing a 'Session not found' that never applied

rules.text: The provider creates daemon sessions with create_session_checked (idx 121, Result<SessionId, String>), never the legacy create_session (idx 3) that answers an empty id on failure
A creation failure fails the open with 'fspec could not create a session: <cause>' and the provider makes no set_session_model or set_thinking_level call for it

examples.text: create_session_checked answers Err('no credentials for provider openai') -> session.open fails with 'fspec could not create a session: no credentials for provider openai'; requests sent: getWorkspaceInfo, listProviders, createSessionChecked only
create_session_checked answers Ok('fspec-sess-42') -> the open proceeds exactly as before (setSessionModel, setThinkingLevel on fspec-sess-42)

architectureNotes.text: server/wire.ts: createSessionChecked 121 (request role: Option<String>; response Result<SessionId, String>). server/session.ts open(): replace createSession with createSessionChecked. test/support/fake-daemon.ts: default handler for createSessionChecked.

FSPEC-040.title: Open the fspec board from the workspace menu on phones
FSPEC-040.description: On phones Paseo's compact tab menu is hard-coded to 'New agent' / 'New terminal' (app compact-workspace-header/tab-switcher.tsx, unchanged at HEAD) and never lists plugin workspace panels, so the board registered in FSPEC-035 had no visible way in on mobile. Plugin header buttons render as rows of the workspace '···' menu on phones (reference.md Header buttons), so the board needs a per-workspace header button.

userStory.role: Paseo user on a phone
userStory.action: open the fspec board from a workspace
userStory.benefit: the board is reachable on mobile, not only on desktop

rules.text: The client watches Paseo's workspace list (workspaces.list with subscribe) and gives each workspace whose directory (workspaceDirectory, else projectRootPath) the fspec daemon serves an 'fspec board' header button that opens the fspec-board panel in that workspace; on phones Paseo shows it as a row of the workspace ··· menu
Whether the daemon serves a directory comes from plugin RPC fspec.board.available({ cwd }) -> { available }, which applies the board's workspace guard and answers false when the daemon is unreachable
A removed workspace loses its button; unloading the plugin removes every button and ends the workspace subscription

examples.text: Workspaces W1 (/ws) and W2 (/other) with the daemon serving /ws -> one header button for W1; pressing it opens panel fspec-board in W1; W2 gets none
workspace_update remove W1 -> W1's button is removed; plugin cleanup -> all buttons removed and the subscription released

architectureNotes.text: shared/board.ts boardAvailableRpc; server/board.ts feed.available(); client/board-buttons.ts syncBoardButtons(deps) with injected list/subscribe, available, addHeaderButton, openPanel (testable without React Native); client/register.ts wires it with client.paseo.workspaces.list({ subscribe: {} }).

FSPEC-041.title: Encode fspec's provider settings and credential RPCs
FSPEC-041.description: Add the daemon's provider-settings, credential, model-cache and OAuth methods (RPC indices 30-38 and 88-101) to the wire codec, with their payload types, verified against Rust-generated golden vectors. Codec only: no plugin behaviour changes.

userStory.role: developer building fspec's provider settings into Paseo
userStory.action: call the daemon's provider-settings, credential, model-cache and OAuth methods through the existing wire codec
userStory.benefit: later stories manage providers without writing any bincode themselves

rules.text: Each new FspecService method uses its fixed tarpc variant index from the Rust trait declaration order: set_default_model=30 … rename_profile=38 and list_provider_credentials=88 … oauth_copilot_device_start=101; arguments are encoded in declaration order with the existing bincode 1.3.3 fixed-width LE conventions.

Every new payload struct (ProviderCredentialInfo, ProviderCredentialInput, TestConnectionResult, OAuthHeadlessStart, OAuthDeviceStart, CustomModelDefinition, ProfileDefinition, ProviderSettingsConfig, ProviderProfileConfig) is encoded/decoded field-for-field in Rust declaration order, re-read from the fspec source at the commit the vectors are generated from.
A service-level Err(String) from the daemon decodes as data ({ ok: false, error }) through the existing Result handling, never as a thrown codec error.
Secret-bearing fields (api_key, custom_api_key, oauth_token, oauth_refresh_token, ProfileDefinition.api_key, pkce_verifier) never appear in any error message or debug string the codec produces.
Codec only: no provider, board or UI behaviour changes in this story.
All 23 now, in one codec pass with one golden-vector run. FSPEC-044 and FSPEC-045 become pure plugin/UI work. This is a deliberate exception to FSPEC-002 rule [1] for this epic.

Golden vectors come from a new binary in the scratch crate /tmp/fspec-golden (outside both repos) that bincode-serializes the real codelet-rpc-types values from the current fspec checkout (path dependency) at the argument/payload level, like the FSPEC-016/023 vectors; variant indices are confirmed against the current trait declaration order. The fspec repo is never modified.

examples.text: set_provider_credentials("anthropic", { kind: "api_key", api_key: Some("sk-ant-test"), all other Options None }) encodes byte-identical to the Rust golden vector.

list_provider_credentials returns two rows — one configured with masked_key Some("sk-ant-••••mnop") and source Some("file"), one unconfigured with both None — and both decode with every field correct.
test_provider_connection decodes Ok({ success: false, error: Some("401 Unauthorized"), latency_ms: 812 }) and, separately, Err("unknown provider") as { ok: false } data.
get_provider_credential decodes both None (unknown provider) and Some(info).
refresh_models_cache("") encodes an empty provider id (all providers) and decodes Ok(Vec<ModelEntry>) with is_custom set on a custom model.
list_provider_settings decodes a ProviderSettingsConfig with zero profiles and one with two profiles, including ProfileDefinition streaming: None vs Some(false).
oauth_copilot_device_start encodes both None and Some("ghe.example.com") and decodes an OAuthDeviceStart with interval 5.
A decode failure while reading a ProviderCredentialInput-bearing frame reports the offset and type but not the api_key bytes.
set_default_model("anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5") encodes byte-identical to the golden vector and decodes Ok(()).
add_custom_model, update_custom_model (with original_model_id) and delete_custom_model encode a CustomModelDefinition with some Options Some and some None, byte-identical to the golden vectors.
save_provider_settings, save_profile, rename_profile and delete_profile encode a ProfileDefinition (base_url, api_key, every optional field) byte-identical to the golden vectors.

oauth_headless_start decodes Ok({ authorize_url, pkce_verifier }); oauth_headless_complete encodes (provider_id, code_with_state, pkce_verifier); oauth_device_start and oauth_device_poll(device_auth_id, interval: u64) round-trip; oauth_get_tokens decodes Ok(true); oauth_clear_tokens and oauth_browser_login decode Ok(()).

questions.text: @human: Encode all 23 methods now, or only the 7 that FSPEC-042 calls (set_default_model, list/get/set/delete_provider_credentials, test_provider_connection, refresh_models_cache), leaving OAuth (094-101) to FSPEC-044 and profiles/custom models (31-38) to FSPEC-045? FSPEC-002 rule [1] says the codec covers only 'the FspecService method payloads the plugin actually calls'.
questions.answer: All 23 now, in one codec pass with one golden-vector run. FSPEC-044 and FSPEC-045 become pure plugin/UI work. This is a deliberate exception to FSPEC-002 rule [1] for this epic.

architectureNotes.text: Same layout as FSPEC-002: the method index map, FspecServiceRequest/response unions, the encoder/decoder switches and the DecodedResponse union in server/wire.ts; payload struct readers/writers next to the existing ProviderInfo/ModelEntry ones. Golden vectors are appended to test/golden/golden-vectors.txt by /tmp/fspec-golden's main.rs; tests extend test/wire.test.ts or a new test/wire-provider-settings.test.ts.

FSPEC-042.title: Serve fspec provider settings to Paseo plugin UI
FSPEC-042.description: Plugin RPCs (shared/settings.ts + server/settings.ts) that list providers with their credential state, save and remove API keys and custom endpoints, test a connection, refresh a provider's model cache and set the default model, then make Paseo refetch the fspec model catalog so the picker reflects the change.

userStory.role: Paseo user running fspec agents
userStory.action: list fspec's providers, add or remove keys, test connections and refresh models through the plugin
userStory.benefit: I can manage fspec's models without opening the fspec TUI, and Paseo's model picker stays in step

rules.text: The settings feed is a plugin-RPC server module (shared/settings.ts schemas + server/settings.ts) built like the board feed: one lazily opened daemon client of its own, registered with server.handle in index.server.ts and closed in the plugin cleanup.
No RPC ever returns a raw key: only masked_key from list_provider_credentials crosses back to the client, and no secret appears in any plugin error, log line or RPC output.
Writes (save key, save custom endpoint, remove, test, refresh models) answer { ok: true, ... } or { ok: false, error } from the daemon's own error text; they never throw into the UI.
When the daemon is unreachable every settings RPC answers { state: 'unavailable', reason } with the same diagnostic the provider status reports.
After any successful write the fspec model catalog Paseo shows reflects the change without restarting Paseo or the plugin.
Allow Remove and override on env/dotenv-sourced rows, with a warning that the key returns when the daemon restarts unless it is removed from the shell environment or .env.

Both: the settings screen refreshes Paseo after its own writes (paseo.providers.refresh), and the fspec provider registers getCatalogCacheKey derived from the daemon's credential state so edits made in the fspec TUI are picked up too.
No default-model control in this story (see the follow-up card that depends on an fspec get_default_model RPC).

settings.list answers the daemon's workspace (get_workspace_info cwd) and one row per provider fspec knows — configured or not, configured first — merged from list_provider_credentials and list_providers: id, display name, configured, credential type, masked key, source, model count, unreachable flag and models.

examples.text: With anthropic configured from file and openai unconfigured, settings.list answers both rows, anthropic first, with anthropic's masked key 'sk-ant-••••mnop' and source 'file' and its 12 models.
Saving an OpenAI key 'sk-proj-abc' answers { ok: true }; the next settings.list shows openai configured with only its masked key, and the response JSON never contains 'sk-proj-abc'.
Saving a custom endpoint for lmstudio sends kind 'custom' with custom_endpoint and custom_api_key, leaving the other fields absent.
Testing anthropic with a bad key answers { ok: true, success: false, error: '401 Unauthorized', latencyMs: 812 }; testing an unknown provider answers { ok: false, error: 'unknown provider' }.
Refreshing anthropic's models answers the new model list; 'Refresh all' sends refresh_models_cache('').
With no daemon.json, settings.list answers { state: 'unavailable', reason: 'no daemon.json found at … — start fspec daemon first' }.
After saving an OpenAI key, a new agent's model picker in Paseo lists OpenAI's models.
Removing an env-sourced openai key answers { ok: true, warning: 'returns when the fspec daemon restarts unless removed from the environment' }.
A key added in the fspec TUI changes the fspec catalog cache key, so Paseo's next catalog lookup re-fetches and shows the new provider's models.

questions.text: @human: Default model: fspec's set_default_model persists a default, but no RPC reads it back, and the plugin always applies the catalog's first model when it opens a session, overriding fspec's default. Drop default-model from this card, or make fspec's default actually drive Paseo (needs a get_default_model RPC added to fspec, or the plugin reading fspec's default-model file)?
questions.answer: Add a get_default_model RPC to fspec so Paseo follows fspec's default. That is fspec-repo work, so it is split out: FSPEC-042 ships without a default-model control, and a new card (Follow fspec's default model in Paseo) depends on the fspec RPC and makes set_default_model + the catalog default work end to end.

questions.text: @human: Env-sourced keys: delete_provider_credentials clears the key from the daemon's own environment, but it returns when the daemon restarts because it comes from the shell. Allow Remove on env/dotenv rows with that warning, or make those rows read-only in Paseo?
questions.answer: Allow Remove and override on env/dotenv-sourced rows, with a warning that the key returns when the daemon restarts unless it is removed from the shell environment or .env.

questions.text: @human: Keeping Paseo's model picker in step: refresh it from the settings screen after its own writes (paseo.providers.refresh), or also make the provider's catalog cache key change whenever fspec's credentials change, so edits made in the fspec TUI show up too (one extra daemon call per catalog lookup)?
questions.answer: Both: the settings screen refreshes Paseo after its own writes (paseo.providers.refresh), and the fspec provider registers getCatalogCacheKey derived from the daemon's credential state so edits made in the fspec TUI are picked up too.

architectureNotes.text: RPCs (shared/settings.ts, defineRpc + zod, like shared/board.ts): fspec.settings.list, fspec.settings.saveCredentials {providerId, kind: api_key|custom, apiKey?, customEndpoint?, customApiKey?}, fspec.settings.removeCredentials, fspec.settings.test, fspec.settings.refreshModels {providerId | ''}. server/settings.ts createSettingsFeed() owns one FspecDaemonClient (lazy, reconnects after connection-lost), registered in index.server.ts. getCatalogCacheKey on the registration in server/provider.ts: a hash of list_provider_credentials (providerId, configured, credentialType, modelCount) + daemon target, undefined when unreachable. The client-side paseo.providers.refresh call after writes belongs to FSPEC-043 (the screen).

FSPEC-043.title: Manage fspec providers from a Paseo settings screen
FSPEC-043.description: A native Paseo settings screen (addSettingsScreen), opened from Paseo Settings, the Command Center and /fspec-settings, that lists fspec's providers and lets you add, change or remove credentials, test a connection, refresh models and pick the default model. Works on desktop and phone widths.

userStory.role: Paseo user running fspec agents
userStory.action: manage fspec's providers from a Paseo settings screen
userStory.benefit: I can add keys, test them and refresh models from desktop or phone without the fspec TUI

rules.text: The screen is a Paseo settings screen (client.addSettingsScreen, id 'fspec-providers', title 'fspec providers') listed under Settings → Plugins; a global Command Center item 'fspec providers' and the slash command /fspec-providers open it with openSettings.
The screen names the daemon workspace it configures; when the daemon is unavailable it shows the feed's reason and a Retry action instead of an empty list.
Keys are typed into secure inputs, never shown back, and cleared after a successful save; the form notes that the key is stored by the fspec daemon on the computer running it.
Remove asks for confirmation naming the provider; removing an environment-sourced key shows the feed's warning that it returns when the daemon restarts.
Test shows the result on the row (connected with latency, or the daemon's error); Refresh shows the new model count; 'Refresh all models' refreshes every provider.
After every successful save, remove or refresh the screen reloads the list and asks Paseo to refresh the fspec provider (paseo.providers.refresh) so the model picker updates.
A failed action leaves the list unchanged and shows the daemon's error on that row.

Providers are one tree in a single card, as in the fspec TUI: configured providers first, then the rest in the daemon's order; each provider header shows ▶/▼, its name and status segments — green '✓ <masked key>' with a dim '[<source>]' for keys, '✓ OAuth [Claude|ChatGPT|GitHub Copilot]' for OAuth sign-ins, gray '(not configured)' otherwise — plus '(N profiles)' when it has profiles and the last test result.

An expanded provider shows a Test and Refresh models action line, then its child rows in the TUI's order: OAuth status and sign-in rows (OAuth providers), '🔑 API key' (API-key providers except openai), '⚙ Settings', one '📁 <profile> → <base URL>' row per profile ('(inherits auth)' when the profile has no base URL), and '+ Add profile'.
Profiles reported by the daemon as their own providers ('<provider>:<profile>', e.g. 'openai:Strata') are folded under their parent provider as profile rows, never listed as separate providers.

Tapping a child row opens its sheet (Paseo Modal, a bottom sheet on phones); this story delivers the API key sheet (masked current key, secure new-key field, Save, Test, Remove). The Settings and profile sheets come with FSPEC-045, OAuth sign-in with FSPEC-044; until then those rows open a sheet that says so.
settings.list also returns each provider's profiles (name and base URL only, from list_provider_settings) so the tree can show them; no profile API key ever reaches the client.

The API key row appears, as in the TUI, for API-key providers except openai (whose keys live in its profiles or the environment); OAuth providers sign in through their OAuth rows, and endpoints are set on profiles (FSPEC-045).

examples.text: Adding a Gemini key 'AIza-test': the key field is secure, Save calls save-credentials with kind api_key, then the list reloads, Paseo's fspec models refresh, and the field is empty again.
Testing anthropic shows 'Connected · 812 ms' or 'Failed: 401 Unauthorized' on the row.
With no daemon running, the screen shows 'no daemon.json found at … — start fspec daemon first' and a Retry action; Retry re-runs the list.
On a phone, Settings → Plugins → fspec for Paseo → fspec providers opens the screen full-screen with Back navigation.

Credentials anthropic (OAuth), openai (key sk-••••abcd from env), openai:Strata and openai:spark (custom) and gemini (unconfigured) become three providers: Anthropic '✓ OAuth [Claude]', OpenAI '✓ sk-••••abcd [env] (2 profiles)' and Gemini '(not configured)'.
Expanded OpenAI shows: Test · Refresh models, ⚙ Settings, 📁 Strata → http://10.0.0.5:8080/v1, 📁 spark → http://spark:8000/v1, + Add profile — and no API key row.
Expanded Anthropic shows: Test · Refresh models, ✓ Logged in [Claude], 🔑 Sign in with browser, 🔑 Sign in with code, ⚙ Settings, + Add profile.
Expanded Gemini shows: 🔑 API key (not set), ⚙ Settings, + Add profile; tapping 🔑 API key opens a sheet with a secure key field.
After a test of Anthropic, its header shows '✓ 812 ms' or '✗ 401 Unauthorized'.

Removing Gemini's key from its API key sheet asks 'Remove the Gemini key from fspec?'; for a key from the environment, a warning then says it returns when the daemon restarts unless removed from the environment.

architectureNotes.text: Client layout mirrors the board: client/settings-model.ts (pure: grouping, row descriptions, which actions a row offers, form validation, result text), client/settings-actions.ts (pure orchestration of a write: call the RPC, then on success reload the list and call paseo.providers.refresh({ providers: ['fspec'] }); on failure return the error and do nothing else), client/settings-screen.tsx (thin React Native component using @getpaseo/plugin/client/ui SettingsSection/SettingsCard/SettingsRow/SettingsInput(secureTextEntry)/SettingsAction, Modal for confirm, useToast, useRpc, usePaseo), registerSettings in client/register.ts wired from index.client.tsx. Paseo owns header, Back, scrolling and the phone full-screen push (public-docs/plugins/reference.md 'Settings screens'). Manual check: open on a phone-width window.

Tree model (client/settings-model.ts): buildTree(providers) folds '<provider>:<profile>' rows into their parent, orders configured first, and yields per-provider header segments and child rows (kind: oauthStatus | oauthLogin | apiKey | settings | profile | addProfile) in the TUI order (rust/fspec-tui/src/views/provider_settings/nav_item.rs build_nav_items, projection.rs oauth_login_methods/oauth_label, row_render.rs icons and tints). Each child row opens a Paseo Modal sheet; the screen keeps one 'open sheet' state.

FSPEC-044.title: Sign in to OAuth providers for fspec from Paseo
FSPEC-044.description: OAuth from each OAuth provider's section, matching the TUI (projection.rs oauth_login_methods): anthropic 'Sign in with browser' / 'Sign in with code' (headless PKCE: open URL, paste code), codex 'Sign in with browser' / 'Sign in with device code', github-copilot 'Sign in with device code' (optional enterprise host), other OAuth providers 'Sign in with browser'. Signed-in providers show 'Logout from OAuth [Claude|ChatGPT|GitHub Copilot]' (oauth_clear_tokens). Browser sign-in opens a browser on the daemon's machine, so it is labelled as such; code/device flows work from any device. Device polling outlives Paseo's 30 s RPC limit via a server-side task + long-poll.

userStory.role: Paseo user running fspec agents
userStory.action: sign fspec in to and out of OAuth providers from the fspec providers screen
userStory.benefit: I can use Claude, ChatGPT and GitHub Copilot subscriptions with fspec without the fspec TUI, even from my phone

rules.text: Each OAuth sign-in row opens its flow in a sheet, as the TUI offers them: 'Sign in with browser' (anthropic, codex, others) starts oauth_browser_login and says it opens a browser on the computer running fspec; 'Sign in with code' (anthropic) shows the sign-in link (oauth_headless_start) and a field to paste the code (oauth_headless_complete); 'Sign in with device code' (codex, github-copilot) shows the code and verification link (oauth_device_start / oauth_copilot_device_start with an optional GitHub Enterprise host) and waits (oauth_device_poll).

A sign-in that waits (browser, device code) runs as a server-side task with a 15-minute daemon deadline; the sheet long-polls its status in holds under Paseo's 30 s RPC limit until it succeeds, fails or is cancelled; closing the sheet or Cancel abandons it and a late result is ignored.
The PKCE verifier and every token stay on the plugin server: the client only ever sees a login id, the link, the user code and the outcome.
The '✓ Logged in [Claude|ChatGPT|GitHub Copilot]' row opens a sheet offering 'Log out', which asks for confirmation and calls oauth_clear_tokens.
After a successful sign-in or log-out the list reloads and Paseo refreshes the fspec provider; a failure shows the daemon's message in the sheet.

examples.text: Anthropic → 'Sign in with code' shows 'Open the sign-in page' (the authorize URL) and a code field; pasting 'abc#state' and Submit calls oauth_headless_complete(anthropic, 'abc#state', <verifier kept on the server>) and the sheet shows 'Signed in to Claude'.
Codex → 'Sign in with device code' shows code ABCD-1234 and https://auth.openai.com/device; the sheet shows 'Waiting for approval…' until oauth_device_poll returns, even past 30 s.
GitHub Copilot → 'Sign in with device code' asks for an optional GitHub Enterprise host first; empty sends None, 'ghe.example.com' sends that host.
Anthropic → 'Sign in with browser' says 'A browser opens on the computer running fspec' and waits for oauth_browser_login.
Closing a device-code sheet before approval ignores the later success; the list is still refreshed on the next reload.
'✓ Logged in [ChatGPT]' → Log out → 'Log out of ChatGPT in fspec?' → oauth_clear_tokens(codex); the header then reads '(not configured)'.

architectureNotes.text: server/oauth.ts (createOAuthLogins(call)): logins keyed by id with state pending | code | succeeded | failed; start(providerId, method, enterpriseHost) runs the daemon calls (long deadline via DaemonConnection.request(message, { deadlineMs })), complete(loginId, code) uses the server-held verifier, status(loginId) long-polls with a 20 s hold (like BOARD_HOLD_MS), cancel(loginId) forgets it. RPCs fspec.settings.oauth-start / oauth-complete / oauth-status / oauth-cancel / oauth-logout. Client: client/oauth-sheet.tsx renders the flow; pure step text in client/settings-model.ts.

FSPEC-045.title: Edit fspec provider settings and profiles from Paseo
FSPEC-045.description: The Settings sheet for EVERY provider (save_provider_settings; fields Context Window … Loop Retries) and the profile sheet (create, edit, rename via rename_profile, delete; Name, Base URL, API Key, then the same fields), matching the fspec TUI's profile_form*.rs: placeholders, defaults (streaming on, max images 4, loop window 160, repeat 10, retries 10, preserve thinking on for anthropic/gemini), parsing and validation messages, compaction threshold '80%' (1-100) or tokens (>= 1000), non-openai profiles inheriting auth. Profile API keys are masked and an unchanged key is kept.

architectureNotes.text: Observed live (FSPEC-042): local-server profiles already appear in list_provider_credentials and list_providers as their own provider rows keyed '<provider>:<profile>' (e.g. 'openai:Strata', credential_type 'custom'), so Paseo catalog ids are 'openai:Strata/<model>'. parseCatalogModelId splits on the first '/', so profile names must not contain '/'. Also: ProfileDefinition has 14 fields (FSPEC-041), not the 7 in this card's research attachment.

Server (server/settings.ts + shared/settings.ts): fspec.settings.provider-settings {providerId} → { settings, profiles: [{ name, definition }] } with every apiKey replaced by apiKeySet; fspec.settings.save-settings {providerId, definition}; fspec.settings.save-profile {providerId, originalName | null, name, definition, apiKey: string | null (null keeps the stored key, read back from list_provider_settings)} → rename_profile when the name changed, else save_profile; fspec.settings.delete-profile {providerId, name}. Client: client/settings-form.ts mirrors rust/fspec-tui/src/views/provider_settings/profile_form.rs, profile_form_context.rs and profile_form_parse.rs (fields, placeholders, defaults, parsing, messages, touched toggles); the screen renders it with SettingsInput / SettingsSwitch in the sheet.

userStory.role: Paseo user running fspec agents
userStory.action: edit every provider's settings and its profiles from the fspec providers screen
userStory.benefit: I can tune context, compaction, streaming, thinking, images and loop detection, and manage endpoints, exactly as in the fspec TUI

rules.text: Every provider's '⚙ Settings' row opens a Settings sheet with the TUI's fields from Context Window on — Context Window, Max Output Tokens, Compaction Threshold, Streaming, Auto-Continue, Preserve Thinking, Max Images, Loop Detection, Loop Window, Loop Repeat, Loop Retries — grouped as Limits, Behaviour and Loop detection, with the TUI's placeholders; Save calls save_provider_settings.

A profile row opens the profile sheet (and '+ Add profile' a new one) with Name, Base URL and API Key followed by the same fields; openai profiles need a Base URL and an API key, other providers' profiles inherit authentication ('Authentication: inherited unless overridden') so both may stay empty; a new openai profile's Base URL starts as http://localhost:8888.

Values are parsed exactly as the TUI does: Context Window and Max Output Tokens are positive whole numbers or empty (Automatic); Compaction Threshold is 'N%' with N 1-100 or a token count of at least 1000, anything else is dropped; Auto-Continue, Max Images, Loop Window, Loop Repeat and Loop Retries are whole numbers or empty; invalid entries show the TUI's message and nothing is saved.
On forms that inherit authentication (provider Settings and non-openai profiles) a toggle is sent only once the user changes it, so untouched toggles keep the daemon's default, as in the TUI.
Profile API keys never reach the client: the sheet shows whether a key is stored; an empty key field keeps the stored key and a typed key replaces it.
Saving a profile under a new name renames it (rename_profile); Delete asks 'Delete the <profile> profile of <provider>?' and calls delete_profile.
After a successful save or delete the list reloads and Paseo refreshes the fspec provider; a failure keeps the sheet open with the daemon's or the parser's message.

Forms are prefilled like the TUI: provider Settings and inherited-auth profiles show stored values, with Max Images and the three loop numbers empty (their placeholders name the defaults) unless set, Streaming and Loop Detection on unless off, and Preserve Thinking on for anthropic and gemini unless set; openai profiles show the effective values (max images 4, window 160, repeat 10, retries 10); a new profile starts with Streaming and Loop Detection on and Preserve Thinking off (shown on for anthropic and gemini).

examples.text: Setting Compaction Threshold '80%' saves compaction_threshold_type 'percentage' value 80; '200000' saves 'tokens' 200000; '500' or '150%' save no threshold.
Context Window 'abc' shows 'Context Window must be a positive whole number, or empty for Automatic' and saves nothing.
Editing OpenAI's Strata profile shows Name 'Strata', Base URL http://10.0.0.5:8080/v1, 'API key stored', and leaving the key empty saves with the stored key.
Renaming Strata to 'Strata2' calls rename_profile(openai, Strata, Strata2, …); deleting spark asks 'Delete the spark profile of OpenAI?' then calls delete_profile(openai, spark).
A new OpenAI profile without a key is not saved ('Enter the Base URL and API key'); a new Anthropic profile named 'fast' with only Context Window 100000 saves with base URL and key empty.
On Gemini's Settings sheet, saving without touching Streaming sends streaming absent; turning it off sends streaming false.

Anthropic's Settings sheet with no stored settings shows Context Window and Max Output Tokens empty ('Automatic (model-specific)'), Streaming on, Preserve Thinking on, Loop Detection on, and Max Images, Loop Window, Loop Repeat and Loop Retries empty with placeholders '4 (default), 0 = no vision', '160 (default)', '10 (default)' and '10 (default), 0 = never retry'.

FSPEC-046.title: Follow fspec's default model in Paseo
FSPEC-046.description: Make fspec's default model drive Paseo: when Paseo opens an fspec agent without an explicit model, use fspec's default (read with get_default_model, variant index 127, Option<String> 'provider/model') instead of the catalog's first model, and offer a 'default model' control in the settings screen that calls set_default_model (idx 30). fspec card RPC-440 delivered get_default_model, appended at index 127 (after the RPC-449 workspace methods 124-126).

userStory.role: Paseo user running fspec agents
userStory.action: have Paseo follow fspec's default model and change that default from the fspec providers screen
userStory.benefit: new agents use the model I chose in fspec instead of whichever model happens to be listed first

rules.text: get_default_model (idx 127, no arguments) answers Option<String> 'provider/model'; the provider reads it for the catalog and for every session.open
The catalog's defaultModel (and isDefault) is fspec's default model when the catalog lists it; otherwise the first reachable model, as before
An agent opened with no explicit or saved model gets fspec's default model; an explicit or saved model still wins and is applied with set_session_model

When fspec has no default model, the model the agent opens with (explicit, saved, else the catalog's first) is made fspec's default with set_default_model before the session is created, as the fspec TUI does when a model is chosen with no session (PROV-118); with no model at all the open fails

create_session_checked answering Ok with an empty id (fspec declined: no default model) fails the open with 'fspec could not create a session: fspec has no default model — choose one under fspec providers' instead of a later 'Session not found'

The fspec providers screen has a Default model row listing every reachable model as provider/model, showing fspec's current default (or 'Not set'); choosing one calls set_default_model (idx 30), then reloads and refreshes Paseo's fspec models

examples.text: get_default_model = Some('openai/gpt-5'), catalog anthropic/claude-sonnet-4, openai/gpt-5 -> catalog defaultModel 'openai/gpt-5' with isDefault on it; Paseo opens an agent with no model -> set_session_model(openai, gpt-5), session.config model 'openai/gpt-5'
get_default_model = None; Paseo opens with model 'openai/gpt-5' -> set_default_model('openai/gpt-5') then create_session_checked, set_session_model(openai, gpt-5)

Settings screen: Default model shows 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-4'; the user picks 'openai/gpt-5' -> fspec.settings.set-default-model { model: 'openai/gpt-5' } -> set_default_model('openai/gpt-5'), list reloads, paseo.providers.refresh(['fspec'])

Golden: get_default_model reply 01 19000000.. 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-4' decodes to model 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-4'; 00 decodes to null; the request is variant index 127 (7f000000) with no argument bytes

architectureNotes.text: server/wire.ts getDefaultModel 127 (request no fields, response Option<String>). server/catalog.ts buildCatalog(providers, defaultModel). server/provider.ts catalog and server/session.ts open() read it; open() calls setDefaultModel (30) only when fspec has none (TUI parity: rust/fspec-tui/src/app/dispatch_model_thinking_dialogs.rs handle_model_selected_no_session) and treats an empty created id as the PROV-101 decline (rust/sessions/src/handle_creation.rs create_session_checked returns Ok(empty) without a default). shared/settings.ts: settings.list gains defaultModel; new fspec.settings.set-default-model RPC. client/settings-model.ts defaultModelChoice (pure); client/settings-screen.tsx a Default model SettingsSelect section.

FSPEC-047.title: Manage fspec custom models from Paseo
FSPEC-047.description: Custom models inside a provider profile (add/update/delete_custom_model with CustomModelDefinition), which the fspec TUI manages from its model selector rather than the provider view. Profiles themselves are delivered by FSPEC-045.

userStory.role: Paseo user running local OpenAI-compatible servers through fspec profiles
userStory.action: add, edit and delete the custom models of an fspec profile from the fspec providers screen
userStory.benefit: models my server offers but fspec cannot discover appear in Paseo's model picker without editing fspec-config.json

rules.text: Custom models belong to a profile of the openai provider (fspec's profile_sections guard rejects any other provider id); the provider tree lists each openai profile's custom models (list_providers entries of key 'openai:<profile>' with is_custom) under its profile row, then '+ Add model to <profile>'

The custom model sheet has the fspec TUI's eight fields (rust/fspec-tui/src/views/model_selector/form_fields.rs): Model ID (required), Display Name, Facade (openai, codex, claude, gemini, zai or default), Context Window, Max Output Tokens, Compaction Trigger ('80%' or '200000'), Reasoning, Vision

Saving builds a CustomModelDefinition like the TUI's build_definition: trimmed id, blank optional fields omitted, a trailing-% trigger is percentage, a bare number is tokens; a blank Model ID or a non-number limit is refused in the form and nothing is sent

A new model is written with add_custom_model (idx 31: 'openai', profile, definition); an edited one with update_custom_model (idx 32) carrying its original id, so renaming the id replaces the entry; delete asks 'Delete the custom model <name> from <profile>?' and calls delete_custom_model (idx 33)
Editing prefills only what list_providers reports (id, display name unless it equals the id, context window, reasoning, vision); facade, max output and trigger start blank, as in the TUI
After every successful write the screen reloads the list and refreshes Paseo's fspec models, so the model appears in the picker; a daemon error is shown on the sheet and changes nothing

examples.text: Profile Strata of openai serves custom model qwen3-coder ('Qwen3 Coder') -> tree rows '📁 Strata → http://10.0.0.5:8080/v1', '◆ Qwen3 Coder', '+ Add model to Strata'

Add: Model ID 'qwen3-coder', Display Name 'Qwen3 Coder', Facade openai, Context Window 32768, Trigger '80%', Reasoning on -> add_custom_model('openai', 'Strata', { id: 'qwen3-coder', displayName: 'Qwen3 Coder', facade: 'openai', contextWindow: 32768, compactionThresholdType: 'percentage', compactionThresholdValue: 80, reasoning: true, hasVision: false })
Edit qwen3 -> id changed to qwen3-coder -> update_custom_model('openai', 'Strata', 'qwen3', { id: 'qwen3-coder', ... })
Delete qwen3-coder -> confirm 'Delete the custom model Qwen3 Coder from Strata?' -> delete_custom_model('openai', 'Strata', 'qwen3-coder')

architectureNotes.text: shared/settings.ts: settingsModelSchema gains optional isCustom/supportsReasoning/supportsVision (set for custom models); saveCustomModelRpc { providerId, profile, originalId, definition } and deleteCustomModelRpc. server/settings.ts: saveCustomModel (originalId null -> addCustomModel, else updateCustomModel) and deleteCustomModel over the FSPEC-041 codec (idx 31-33). client/custom-model-form.ts (pure: fields, prefill, build, prompts); client/settings-model.ts tree rows customModel/addCustomModel under openai profiles; client/custom-model-sheet.tsx; client/settings-screen.tsx wires the sheet. The plugin sends provider id 'openai' (the daemon guard in rust/sessions/src/handle_impl/handle_impl_6.rs); the fspec TUI's model selector passes the profile's list_providers key ('openai:<profile>', profile_sections.rs build_profile_provider_info), which that guard rejects — reported, not worked around in fspec.

FSPEC-048.title: Show work unit details in a drawer over the fspec board
FSPEC-048.description: Clicking a card's details opens a drawer that slides in from the right over the top of the board, covering part of it (the board dimmed behind; tap outside, Back or Close dismisses it), instead of the bottom sheet / centered dialog. It follows Paseo's plugin design rules (theme colours, compact padding, host ScrollView) and clears Android's navigation bar.

userStory.role: Paseo user working an fspec board
userStory.action: see a card's full details and actions in a drawer that slides over the board
userStory.benefit: I can read and act on a work unit without leaving the board or opening another view, on desktop and phone

rules.text: The drawer opens straight onto the card's full fspec record (get_work_unit_details): nothing else needs to be opened to see it, and while it loads the board snapshot's id, title, status, epic, estimate and description show at once.
The card's actions sit at the top of the drawer, under the title: Open in agent, Move up and Move down (not for done cards), and Close.

The record is laid out as formatted blocks, not raw lines: a header (id, title, and chips for type, status, epic, estimate); Description; User Story (As a / I want / So that); numbered Rules; Examples; Questions with their answers (open ones marked); Assumptions; Architecture Notes; Event Storm grouped by kind; Relationships as tappable work-unit chips; Attachments; a status History timeline; and Accounting, Timestamps and any other fields as label/value rows. Deleted items are hidden; empty blocks are omitted.

Reserve a fixed Android bottom inset of 48dp (3-button navigation bar height; also clears gesture navigation) in the drawer, and apply the same bottom clearance to the board's own scrolling lists (search results and card columns). No Paseo SDK change.

This replaces FSPEC-036's details strip and details sheet: its scenarios 'The details strip shows the selected card' and 'Full details are projected like the TUI document' are retired together with detailsStrip, projectDetails, DetailsStrip and DetailsDialog; the drawer's document (which keeps unknown fields and groups the event storm) supersedes them, and FSPEC-036's details RPC stays.

Selecting a card opens a drawer that slides in from the right over the top of the board, covering part of it; the board is not dimmed and stays usable beside it (scrolling, searching, column chips); selecting another card shows that card in the drawer. The drawer's Close button, Android Back or web Escape closes it and clears the selection.

The drawer keeps a history of the work units it showed: selecting a card on the board starts a new history with that card; tapping a relationship chip shows that work unit and adds it after the current one (dropping any forward entries); back and forward arrows in the drawer header step through the history and are disabled at either end.
