Width: 88% of the board (at most 480) on compact layouts, otherwise 45% (between 360 and 560); the drawer follows Paseo's plugin design rules: theme colours only (surface1 panel with a border on its left edge and no shadow, foreground / foregroundMuted text, accent chips), tighter padding when compact, and the host ScrollView for its body.

Each attachment is a link that opens the file in Paseo's file viewer: it is rendered through the plugin Markdown component as a link to the file's absolute path (the daemon workspace joined with the attachment path), which Paseo's workspace file-link resolver opens; the link text is the file name, with its folder shown beneath.

questions.text: @human: Clearing Android's navigation bar: plugins cannot read safe-area insets (react-native-safe-area-context is not in the plugin runtime and the plugin API exposes none), while Paseo's own panels pad with useSafeAreaInsets. Reserve a fixed Android bottom inset in the drawer now, add an insets API to Paseo's plugin SDK first (a Paseo change), or both?
questions.answer: Reserve a fixed Android bottom inset of 48dp (3-button navigation bar height; also clears gesture navigation) in the drawer, and apply the same bottom clearance to the board's own scrolling lists (search results and card columns). No Paseo SDK change.

examples.text: Tapping RPC-347 on the board slides in a drawer showing 'RPC-347 — Backend custom-model RPC + NAPI surface', chips story · done · rust-frontend · 8 pts, then Open in agent / Close at the top (no Move buttons: it is done).

RPC-347's drawer lists its 9 rules numbered 1-9, its 8 examples, 3 architecture notes, the user story as 'As a model-selector UI… / I want to add, update, and delete custom… / So that the custom-model write path…', Depends On chips RPC-346 and one more, 2 attachments and a 10-step status history.
Tapping the RPC-346 chip in RPC-347's drawer shows RPC-346 in the same drawer.
A question with an answer reads 'Should we…?' with 'Answer: …' under it; an unanswered one is marked Open.
On an Android phone the drawer's last block and the board's last card sit above the navigation bar.

With RPC-347's drawer open, the board can still be scrolled and searched, and tapping RPC-440 on the board shows RPC-440 in the drawer; Close, Android Back or Escape closes it and clears the selection.

From RPC-347, tapping the Relates To chip RPC-440 then its Depends On chip RPC-346 gives history RPC-347 › RPC-440 › RPC-346: back shows RPC-440, back again RPC-347 (back now disabled), forward shows RPC-440; tapping a new chip RPC-300 there drops RPC-346 from the forward history.
Selecting RPC-500 on the board while the drawer shows RPC-346 starts a fresh history with only RPC-500 (both arrows disabled).

RPC-347's attachment 'spec/attachments/RPC-347/ast-research.md' in workspace /Users/me/fspec shows as the link 'ast-research.md' to /Users/me/fspec/spec/attachments/RPC-347/ast-research.md; tapping it opens the file in Paseo.

architectureNotes.text: client/details-document.ts (pure): documentFor(record, unit) → header {id, title, chips} + blocks of kinds text | userStory | numbered | list | questions | storm | links | attachments | history | fields, ported from details-model.ts SECTIONS / STORM_GROUPS / humanize with deleted items dropped; drawerGeometry(boardWidth, compact) → width; ANDROID_BOTTOM_INSET = 48 and bottomInset(platform). client/details-drawer.tsx: absolute overlay inside the board root (backdrop Pressable + right-anchored Animated.View translateX, native driver), header + actions, body in host ScrollView with contentContainerStyle paddingBottom = inset; BackHandler / Escape close. board-panel.tsx: selection opens the drawer; the DetailsStrip and DetailsDialog are removed; board lists get the same bottom inset.

FSPEC-049.title: Decode fspec's WorkspaceWorkUnitsUpdate envelope instead of dropping it
FSPEC-049.description: fspec RPC-445 appended Envelope variant 9 WorkspaceWorkUnitsUpdate(WorkspaceWorkUnits { workspace: String, units: Vec<WorkUnitInfo> }): work-unit pushes for workspaces the daemon opened besides its start workspace, fanned out to every full-surface connection (rust/rpc-server/src/workspace_fanout.rs, server/connection_fanouts.rs). server/wire.ts decodeEnvelope rejects every index above 8 with 'unknown Envelope variant index 9', so server/daemon.ts throws the frame away and the push never reaches the board; any caller decoding frames directly fails outright.

rules.text: The codec decodes and encodes Envelope variant index 9 WorkspaceWorkUnitsUpdate(WorkspaceWorkUnits { workspace: String, units: Vec<WorkUnitInfo> }) byte-exactly; only indices 10 and above are unknown
The daemon client hands a WorkspaceWorkUnitsUpdate push to its envelope listeners like any other push; it is never dropped as undecodable
Consumers that do not use workspace pushes ignore them: the provider's sessions are untouched and the board of the daemon's start workspace keeps its units and revision

examples.text: Golden vector: Envelope 09000000 + 02000000000000002f770000000000000000 decodes to { kind: workspaceWorkUnitsUpdate, workspace: '/w', units: [] } and encodes back to the same bytes
The board of /work is at revision r; the daemon pushes WorkspaceWorkUnitsUpdate for /other with one unit; a held watch for /work keeps holding and its next answer still shows /work's units

architectureNotes.text: server/wire.ts: WorkspaceWorkUnitsUpdateEnvelope { kind: 'workspaceWorkUnitsUpdate', workspace, units }, ENVELOPE_NAMES/envelopeVariantIndex/encode/decode gain index 9 (fspec rust/rpc-server/src/envelope.rs; rpc-types chrome.rs WorkspaceWorkUnits). The daemon fans it out to every full-surface connection (rpc-server/src/server/connection_fanouts.rs -> workspace_fanout.rs), only for workspaces opened besides the start workspace (the start workspace keeps WorkUnitsUpdate). server/board.ts ignores it for now; FSPEC-053 serves those workspaces' boards.

FSPEC-050.title: Decode PauseState's details and real tool_call_id and attach the approval to its gated tool call
FSPEC-050.description: fspec BUG-291 renamed PauseState's third field (which carried the pause details text under the name tool_call_id) to details and appended a real tool_call_id: the id of the streamed ToolCall chunk that raised the pause. server/wire.ts still decodes the 3-field layout, so get_pause_state (idx 80) leaves the 4th field unread and the old golden vectors no longer match the daemon. The approval request is still attached to whichever tool call happens to be running (FSPEC-016's workaround, transcript.runningToolCall) instead of the call the pause gates.

rules.text: get_pause_state (idx 80) decodes Option<PauseState { kind, prompt, details: Option<String>, tool_call_id: Option<String> }> in that field order (fspec BUG-291): details is the pause details text, tool_call_id the id of the streamed ToolCall that raised the pause

When a paused session's snapshot holds an approval pause, the provider reads get_pause_state for its tool_call_id and builds the permission from that tool call: its name and detail, and metadata.toolCallId; the request is still answered by the snapshot's request_id
When get_pause_state has no tool_call_id, names a call the transcript never saw, or fails, the permission falls back to the most recent running tool call as before
The permission description is the pause message plus its details text (the snapshot's details, or PauseState.details when the snapshot has none)

examples.text: Bash call-1 'ps -axo pid' and Read call-2 are both running; Paused; get_pause_state = Triple 'Bash: risky', details 'rm -rf build', tool_call_id 'call-1' -> permission name Bash, detail shell 'ps -axo pid', metadata { toolCallId: 'call-1' }

Golden: 01 01000000 'Bash: risky' 01 'rm -rf build' 01 'call-1' decodes to { kind: triple, prompt: 'Bash: risky', details: 'rm -rf build', toolCallId: 'call-1' }; Confirm 'ok?' with neither ends 00 00

architectureNotes.text: server/wire.ts PauseState gains details; read/write 4 fields. server/session.ts openPause: after get_interaction_snapshot (still the source of request_id and the answer path, FSPEC-018) call getPauseState for the gated tool call id. server/transcript.ts gains toolCall(callId) -> { name, detail }. Supersedes FSPEC-016 rule 5 (tool_call_id carried the details text on fspec 0.10.9 before BUG-291). The interaction snapshot JSON (sessions/src/background_session/interactions.rs interaction_snapshot) carries no tool call id, so get_pause_state is the only source.

FSPEC-051.title: Steer and queue prompts through fspec's submit_input
FSPEC-051.description: fspec RIG-016 added submit_input (idx 128: session_id, text, InputMode Steer|Queue|Interrupt). Advertise Paseo's prompt.steer: delivery 'steer' joins the running turn with submit_input Steer (prompt_result { type: 'steer', turnId }); a prompt that arrives while a turn runs is handed to the daemon with submit_input Queue so fspec holds and orders it, instead of relying on send_input's implicit queue. An interrupted turn now leaves queued inputs parked (Interrupted.queued_inputs) instead of dropping them: the plugin reports them and runs them on the next prompt rather than cancelling their turns.

userStory.role: Paseo user directing a busy fspec agent
userStory.action: steer the running turn or queue a follow-up, with fspec holding and ordering what I send
userStory.benefit: I can correct the agent mid-turn and nothing I queued is lost when I stop it

rules.text: submit_input (idx 128: session_id, text, mode InputMode Steer=0 | Queue=1 | Interrupt=2) answers Result<(), String>; an unknown session answers Err('Session not found: <id>')
The provider advertises Paseo's prompt.steer capability

A delivery 'steer' prompt while a turn runs is sent with submit_input Steer and answered with session.prompt_result { type: 'steer', turnId: <running turn> }; it starts no turn, and the daemon's immediate UserInput echo carries the prompt's clientMessageId
A delivery 'steer' prompt with no running turn, or one the daemon rejects, is answered with session.prompt_result failed and starts no turn
With clearPendingPermissions, the steer is submitted first and then the approval pause or stdin question blocking the turn is denied, so the turn can reach the point where fspec reads the steer

A delivery 'auto' prompt while a turn runs is handed to fspec with submit_input Queue (fspec holds and orders it) and becomes the next turn, started only when every earlier turn settled; an idle session's prompt still uses send_input

A steer the turn never reached starts as its own daemon turn after the turn completes, ahead of queued prompts (fspec continue_with_inbox): the provider runs it as an extra turn, recognised by the daemon's UserInput not matching the next queued prompt

Interrupted/InterruptedWithReason cancels only the running turn: queued prompts stay parked in fspec (listed in queued_inputs), their turns are not started, and the provider shows a notice listing them; the next prompt is submitted with submit_input Queue so fspec runs the parked prompts first, each as its own turn, then the new one

examples.text: turn-1 running; Paseo steers 'use the staging database' -> submit_input(s, 'use the staging database', Steer); prompt_result { type: steer, turnId: turn-1 }; UserInput 'use the staging database' -> user_message with that clientMessageId; Done -> turn-1 completed
turn-1 running, Paseo sends 'b' (auto) -> submit_input(s, 'b', Queue), prompt_result turn-2; Done -> turn-1 completed, turn-2 started

turn-1 running, 'b' queued (turn-2); Stop -> InterruptedWithReason { queued_inputs: ['b'] } -> turn-1 canceled, turn-2 not started, notice '1 queued prompt is waiting'; Done -> nothing; Paseo sends 'c' -> submit_input(s, 'c', Queue), prompt_result turn-3, turn-2 started; Done -> turn-2 completed, turn-3 started
turn-1 running, 'b' queued; steer 's' never reached; Done -> turn-1 completed; UserInput 's' -> turn-3 started (extra turn); Done -> turn-3 completed, turn-2 started

architectureNotes.text: server/wire.ts submitInput 128 + InputMode table (rpc-types input_mode.rs). server/provider.ts capabilities += prompt.steer. server/session.ts: QueuedTurn gains text and parked; prompt() routes delivery steer / auto-while-busy / parked-resume; settle() watches for a steer overflow turn; handleChunk interrupts park the queue. Semantics: fspec rust/sessions/src/background_session/input_modes.rs submit_input (idle Queue resumes parked inputs ahead of it), rust/agent-loop/src/agent_loop/finalization.rs start_queued_input (an interrupted turn leaves the inbox parked), rust/cli/src/interactive/stream_loop/steer.rs (steer delivered at a safe boundary, no chunk), interrupted.rs (queued_inputs reported without draining). Matches the fspec TUI (agent-view-steer-and-queue-keys.feature): Enter steers and Alt+Enter queues while a turn runs; an idle Enter still sends a normal turn.

FSPEC-052.title: Run each Paseo agent in its own workspace on a multi-workspace fspec daemon
FSPEC-052.description: One fspec daemon can serve several workspaces (RPC-441..445): create_session_in_workspace (idx 126: workspace, role) runs a session in the named workspace, list_workspaces (idx 124) lists the ones it serves. Replace FSPEC-015's refusal of Paseo directories outside the daemon's start workspace: an agent in another directory gets a session in that workspace; the start workspace keeps create_session_checked. A workspace the daemon refuses fails the open with the daemon's reason.

userStory.role: Paseo user with projects in several directories
userStory.action: open an fspec agent in any of my Paseo workspaces against one fspec daemon
userStory.benefit: each agent works in its own project without starting a daemon per directory

rules.text: list_workspaces (idx 124) answers Result<Vec<WorkspaceEntry { path, name, start }>, String> with the start workspace first; create_session_in_workspace (idx 126: workspace: String, role: Option<String>) answers Result<SessionId, String> and opens the workspace on the daemon if needed

session.open resolves its workspace from list_workspaces: the deepest listed workspace holding the Paseo cwd (realpaths, as FSPEC-015 compared them); a cwd no listed workspace holds becomes its own workspace

An agent in the daemon's start workspace (or a directory inside it) is created with create_session_checked as before; an agent in any other workspace is created with create_session_in_workspace(<workspace path>, role)

When create_session_in_workspace fails (for example 'workspace path is not a directory: <path>'), the open fails with 'fspec could not create a session in <workspace>: <reason>' and nothing is configured

Paseo's import list for a cwd lists the sessions of the listed workspace holding it (list_sessions(<workspace path>)); a cwd no listed workspace holds lists nothing, and no workspace is opened just to list it

examples.text: Daemon started in /repos/fspec lists [/repos/fspec (start)]; Paseo opens an agent in /repos/fspec-paseo -> create_session_in_workspace('/repos/fspec-paseo', None); the open reaches ready (FSPEC-015 used to refuse it)
Listed /repos/fspec (start) and /repos/app; agent in /repos/app/web -> create_session_in_workspace('/repos/app', None)
Agent in /repos/fspec/rust -> create_session_checked(None) as before
create_session_in_workspace answers Err('workspace path is not a directory: /gone') -> request.failed 'fspec could not create a session in /gone: workspace path is not a directory: /gone'
Golden: list_workspaces Ok([{/w/a, a, true}, {/w/b, b, false}]); create_session_in_workspace args ('/w/b', Some('role')) and reply Ok('s-9'); list_workspace_work_units args ('/w/b')

architectureNotes.text: server/wire.ts listWorkspaces 124 (WorkspaceEntry rpc-types chrome.rs), listWorkspaceWorkUnits 125, createSessionInWorkspace 126. server/session.ts: workspaceFor(cwd) replaces the FSPEC-015 refusal; open() picks create_session_checked or create_session_in_workspace; list() lists the resolved workspace. fspec side: rpc service_implementation/schedule_loops.rs create_session_in_workspace (opens the workspace through SharedFspecService::workspace, registry RPC-441), sessions/src/default_project.rs create_session_in_workspace_checked (canonicalises, rejects non-directories, needs a default model). TUI parity (board-workspace-dropdown.feature): session creation uses create_session_in_workspace when a non-start workspace is selected. A Paseo cwd inside a listed workspace maps to that workspace rather than opening a nested one.

FSPEC-053.title: Show the fspec board for every workspace the daemon serves
FSPEC-053.description: The board, its availability check and the phone menu entry only exist for the daemon's start workspace. Use list_workspaces (idx 124) and list_workspace_work_units (idx 125) to serve the board of any listed workspace, kept live by WorkspaceWorkUnitsUpdate pushes (envelope 9, FSPEC-049).

userStory.role: Paseo user with several projects on one fspec daemon
userStory.action: see the live fspec board of whichever served workspace I am in, on desktop and phone
userStory.benefit: every project's board is one tap away without restarting the daemon in it

rules.text: The board serves a cwd held by any workspace list_workspaces lists (deepest match); the start workspace's board comes from the connect-time WorkUnitsUpdate and later WorkUnitsUpdate pushes, any other workspace's from list_workspace_work_units (idx 125) on first watch and WorkspaceWorkUnitsUpdate pushes (envelope 9) tagged with its path
A push for one workspace changes only that workspace's board: watches of other workspaces keep holding; pushes for workspaces no panel has loaded are ignored
A workspace's board shows the focus of the sessions whose project is that workspace (SessionInfo.project from the snapshot and Created events); sessions of other workspaces are left out
fspec.board.available answers true for a cwd held by any served workspace, so the phone '···' menu entry appears for every served workspace, not only the start workspace
A cwd no served workspace holds answers unavailable 'the fspec daemon serves <paths>, not <cwd> — start fspec in <cwd> to use it there' and is never opened as a workspace by the board

Card details (get_work_unit_details) and Move up/down (move_work_unit_up/down) read and write the daemon's start workspace only, so on another workspace's board they answer 'card details and moves are only available in the fspec daemon's start workspace (<start>)'

examples.text: Daemon started in /ws also serves /app; watch { cwd: '/app/web' } -> list_workspace_work_units('/app') -> ready, workspace '/app', units [APP-001]
Held watch on /app; push WorkspaceWorkUnitsUpdate('/app', [APP-002]) -> answers APP-002; push WorkUnitsUpdate (start) -> /app's board unchanged
Sessions s-ws (project /ws, focused FSPEC-001) and s-app (project /app, focused APP-001) -> /app's focus { APP-001: [s-app] }
available('/app/web') -> true, available('/other') -> false

architectureNotes.text: server/board.ts keeps one board per served workspace path (units + revision), a session -> project map, and per-workspace waiters; watch/available/details/move resolve the cwd with server/workspaces.ts servingWorkspace over list_workspaces. Boards of non-start workspaces load with list_workspace_work_units (which opens the workspace and makes the daemon push WorkspaceWorkUnitsUpdate for it, fspec RPC-445 workspace_fanout.rs) and stay live from those pushes. get_work_unit_details and move_work_unit_up/down take no workspace and act on the daemon's cwd (rpc service_implementation schedule_loops.rs / workspace_history.rs), so they are refused off the start workspace rather than answering for the wrong project. TUI parity: board-workspace-dropdown.feature (WorkUnitsLoaded from the start stream is dropped while another workspace is selected; WorkspaceWorkUnitsLoaded applies only to the selected path; sessions shown per workspace by project). The client is unchanged: the panel and the phone entry already go through watch/available.

FSPEC-054.title: Find the right local fspec daemon and authenticate to it
FSPEC-054.description: Every local fspec daemon now advertises itself in daemons/<pid>.json beside daemon.json (RPC-446), and daemon.json names one live daemon, no longer the last one started (BUG-289). Read the live entries, prefer the daemon whose workspace holds the Paseo directory, and fall back to daemon.json. A daemon started with FSPEC_DAEMON_TOKEN requires 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' on every WebSocket upgrade (RPC-447): send it when the plugin sees FSPEC_DAEMON_TOKEN. The loopback-only rule stays.

userStory.role: Paseo user running more than one fspec daemon, possibly token-protected
userStory.action: have the plugin find the daemon serving my project and authenticate to it
userStory.benefit: agents and boards reach the right daemon without FSPEC_DAEMON_URL, and protected daemons accept the plugin

rules.text: Every local daemon advertises itself in daemons/<pid>.json beside daemon.json (/fspec/daemons or ~/.fspec/daemons, daemon.json schema: port, pid, workspace, started_at, version); entries that cannot be read or whose pid is not alive are ignored

A daemon client is bound to the daemon chosen for the first Paseo directory it serves: the live entry whose workspace holds the directory (deepest match), else the live daemon daemon.json names, else the live entry with the lowest pid; FSPEC_DAEMON_URL still wins over all of them and the availability probe uses the same order without a directory

The provider connection hints its client with the directory of the first catalog, sessions or session.open input that carries one; the board picks a daemon for each panel directory the same way, one board connection per daemon
With neither a live daemon.json nor a live entry, discovery reports the same diagnostics as before (missing or stale daemon.json, which is still removed when its pid is dead)

When FSPEC_DAEMON_TOKEN is set (non-empty) in the Paseo daemon's environment, every WebSocket upgrade carries 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'; without it no Authorization header is sent; a daemon armed with a token answers a missing or wrong bearer with HTTP 401 (fspec RPC-447)
The loopback-only rule is unchanged: a discovered port is always dialled on 127.0.0.1 and FSPEC_DAEMON_URL must name a loopback host; a failed connect names FSPEC_DAEMON_TOKEN as something to check

examples.text: daemon.json names pid 100 (workspace /a, port 4100); daemons/200.json is live with workspace /b, port 4200; an agent opens in /b/web -> the provider connects to ws://127.0.0.1:4200/
Same files, agent in /c -> ws://127.0.0.1:4100/ (daemon.json)
No daemon.json; daemons/111.json (dead pid, workspace /p) and daemons/222.json (live, workspace /other) -> directory /p connects to 222's port
FSPEC_DAEMON_TOKEN=s3cret -> the socket is opened with headers { Authorization: 'Bearer s3cret' }

architectureNotes.text: server/daemon.ts: liveDaemonEntries(dir) reads daemons/*.json (fspec rust/fspec/src/common/daemon_registry.rs list_live_daemons; the plugin ignores dead entries instead of deleting them, leaving that to fspec), resolveTarget picks entry/daemon.json/lowest pid with a workspace hint set by preferWorkspace(cwd) (first one wins, before the first connect); openSocket(url, { headers }) with Authorization from FSPEC_DAEMON_TOKEN (fspec rust/rpc/src/auth_token.rs, rpc-server/src/client/connect.rs); the default transport passes headers to Node's undici WebSocket. server/provider.ts dispatch hints the daemon client. server/board.ts createBoardFeed routes each cwd to a per-daemon board feed pinned with connectUrl. daemon.json now names one live daemon and is never overwritten by a second one (BUG-289), so it is the right fallback.

FSPEC-055.title: Start fspec orchestrator bots from Paseo with a bot mode
FSPEC-055.description: The fspec TUI's New Bot (TUI-114) creates a session whose role is the orchestrator role from rust/sessions/src/bot.rs ORCHESTRATOR_ROLE (first line '# fspec bot: orchestrator'); a session is a bot iff its role starts with that marker. Expose Paseo provider modes 'agent' (default) and 'bot'; a bot agent's daemon session is created with that role on both creation paths, and a resumed or imported session whose role is a bot role shows as bot mode.

userStory.role: Paseo user who wants fspec to orchestrate work
userStory.action: start an fspec orchestrator bot from Paseo by choosing a bot mode
userStory.benefit: one agent breaks my request into tasks, runs sub-agents on them and reports back, as New Bot does in the fspec TUI

rules.text: The provider offers Paseo modes 'agent' (Agent, the default) and 'bot' (Bot) in its catalog and every session.config

A new session opened in mode 'bot' is created with fspec's orchestrator role (rust/sessions/src/bot.rs ORCHESTRATOR_ROLE, copied verbatim) on both creation paths: create_session_checked(Some(role)) in the start workspace and create_session_in_workspace(workspace, Some(role)) elsewhere; mode 'agent' or none creates it with no role

A session is a bot iff its role starts with '# fspec bot: orchestrator'; a resumed or imported session reads its role with get_session_role (idx 44) and its committed mode is 'bot' for a bot role, otherwise 'agent', whatever mode Paseo asked for
session.configure with mode 'bot' sets the orchestrator role with set_session_role (idx 45); with mode 'agent' it clears a bot role (set_session_role None) and leaves any other role alone
An unknown mode fails the open or configure with 'invalid fspec mode "<mode>" — expected agent or bot'
The import list marks bot sessions: their description starts with 'Bot · '

examples.text: Paseo opens an agent in /work with mode 'bot' -> create_session_checked(Some(ORCHESTRATOR_ROLE)); session.config mode 'bot'
Paseo opens a bot in /repos/app (not the start workspace) -> create_session_in_workspace('/repos/app', Some(ORCHESTRATOR_ROLE))
Reopening fspec-sess-42 whose get_session_role is the orchestrator role -> session.config mode 'bot'
configure { mode: 'agent' } on a bot -> set_session_role(fspec-sess-42, None); session.config mode 'agent'

architectureNotes.text: server/bot.ts: ORCHESTRATOR_ROLE (verbatim from fspec rust/sessions/src/bot.rs, TUI-114), BOT_ROLE_MARKER, isBotRole, FSPEC_MODES. server/wire.ts getSessionRole 44 (SessionId) -> Option<String>, setSessionRole 45 (SessionId, Option<String>) -> Result<(), String>. server/catalog.ts publishes the modes and defaultMode 'agent'; server/session.ts open() passes the role to createDaemonSession, reads the role of a resumed session, configure() maps mode to set_session_role, list() marks bot sessions from SessionInfo.role. TUI parity: New Bot creates the session with the role and no other engine change; the agent bar marks bot sessions from SessionInfo.role. The daemon's role decides a resumed session's mode, so an import with Paseo's default mode never strips a bot's role.

FSPEC-056.title: Decode ProviderInfo's provider_id and name the base provider in custom-model writes
FSPEC-056.description: fspec BUG-325 appended provider_id (the base provider) as ProviderInfo's last field, so the plugin's ProviderInfo reader is one field short and every list_providers reply after the first section misdecodes. The settings tree also derives a profile's base provider by splitting the section key at ':' and assumes 'openai' for custom-model writes. Decode provider_id, fold profile sections by provider_id/profile_name, send provider_id in add/update/delete_custom_model, and surface every refused custom-model write (fspec now refuses missing profiles, unknown model ids and non-openai providers).

rules.text: ProviderInfo is { key, display_name, models, profile_name, is_unreachable, provider_id } (fspec BUG-325): provider_id, the base provider, is read and written last
A settings row carries its base provider (providerId) and profile (profileName): from ProviderInfo for list_providers rows, the row's own id and no profile for list_provider_credentials rows
The provider tree folds a profile section under the provider its providerId names, as the profile its profileName names; section keys are never parsed
add/update/delete_custom_model send the profile section's providerId; every write the daemon refuses (missing profile, unknown model id, non-openai provider) is shown on the sheet and changes nothing

examples.text: ProviderInfo{'openai:lab','OpenAI: lab',[],Some('lab'),false,'openai'} <-> golden provider_info_profile; ProviderInfo{'anthropic','Anthropic',[],None,false,'anthropic'} <-> provider_info_cloud
A list_providers section keyed 'lab-section' with providerId 'openai' and profileName 'Lab' folds under OpenAI as profile Lab; its custom models show under Lab
delete_custom_model answers "Model 'qwen3' not found in profile 'Strata'" -> the sheet shows it, the list is not reloaded

architectureNotes.text: server/wire.ts ProviderInfo.providerId (read/write last). shared/settings.ts settingsProviderSchema gains providerId and profileName. server/settings.ts list fills them. client/settings-model.ts buildTree folds by providerId/profileName; customModel/addCustomModel rows and the customModel sheet carry the section's providerId, which client/settings-screen.tsx sends.

FSPEC-057.title: Surface refused input and resume reattached sessions explicitly
FSPEC-057.description: fspec BUG-328: send_input (idx 4) and send_input_with_thinking (idx 46) return Result<(), String> and the daemon accepts input only for a session it holds live (no implicit resume inside send_input/submit_input). The plugin decodes no payload for send_input and ignores errors, so a refused prompt waits forever. Decode the Result and fail the turn with the daemon's reason; every path that reattaches to an existing daemon session (resume, import) resumes it with resume_session before input and fails the open when the resume fails instead of silently starting a new session.

rules.text: send_input (idx 4) and send_input_with_thinking (idx 46) answer Result<(), String> (fspec BUG-328); an Err fails the prompt's turn with the daemon's reason

fspec accepts input only for a session it holds live; every path that reattaches to an existing daemon session (reopen and import, both session.open with persistence) calls resume_session before the session takes input
A failed resume_session fails the open with 'fspec could not resume session <id>: <reason>'; no new daemon session is created in its place

examples.text: send_input answers Err('Session not found: s-1') -> golden send_input_err; the turn fails with 'fspec daemon send_input failed: Session not found: s-1'

Reopen with persistence { sessionId: 'gone-1' } and resume_session Err('Failed to load session manifest: not found') -> request.failed 'fspec could not resume session gone-1: Failed to load session manifest: not found', no create_session

architectureNotes.text: server/wire.ts sendInput/sendInputWithThinking replies decode Result<void> (encoded with the Result<void> group). server/session.ts prompt unwraps send_input; open() throws when resume() fails instead of creating a session and posting a warning notice. test/support/fake-daemon.ts answers send_input Ok by default.

FSPEC-058.title: Card details and reordering act on the board's workspace
FSPEC-058.description: fspec RPC-450: get_work_unit_details, move_work_unit_up and move_work_unit_down take (workspace, id); an unknown workspace is an error. The plugin sends (id) only and refuses details and moves outside the daemon's start workspace (FSPEC-053). Send the board panel's served workspace for every board, drop the start-only refusal, and drop the get_workspace_info fallback when list_workspaces fails or is empty.

rules.text: get_work_unit_details (idx 123), move_work_unit_up (18) and move_work_unit_down (19) take (workspace, id) (fspec RPC-450); the board sends the served workspace holding the panel's cwd, for the start workspace and every other served workspace alike
The start-workspace-only refusal of details and moves (FSPEC-053) is removed
A list_workspaces error, an empty list or a list without a start workspace is an error with that reason for the board and for opening an agent; get_workspace_info is never used in its place
A session whose project the board does not know shows on no workspace's board

examples.text: Panel of /app/web: details APP-001 -> get_work_unit_details('/app', 'APP-001'); Move up -> move_work_unit_up('/app', 'APP-001'); args bytes = golden work_unit_details_args for ('/w/b', 'AUTH-001')

list_workspaces answers Err('workspace registry unavailable: locked') -> watch unavailable 'fspec daemon list_workspaces failed: workspace registry unavailable: locked'; open fails with the same reason

architectureNotes.text: server/wire.ts: getWorkUnitDetails/moveWorkUnitUp/moveWorkUnitDown requests { workspace, id }. server/board.ts details/move pass found.entry.path, startOnly removed; workspaces() throws on Err/empty/no start; workspaceOf unknown project -> null. server/session.ts workspaces() throws the same way.

FSPEC-059.title: Attach approval pauses to their tool call by id only
FSPEC-059.description: FSPEC-050 attaches a pause without a tool_call_id to the most recent running tool call, a guess that can attach the approval to the wrong call. Attach by get_pause_state's tool_call_id only; without one the approval is shown unattached. A failed get_pause_state or get_interaction_snapshot read is reported to the user instead of being swallowed.

rules.text: An approval is attached only to the tool call get_pause_state's tool_call_id names (shell detail and metadata.toolCallId from that call); with no id, or an id the transcript does not know, it is shown unattached: name and description from the snapshot, no detail, no metadata

A pause the provider cannot read (get_interaction_snapshot or get_pause_state failing, or a pause kind other than Confirm, Triple or Continue) is reported as an error notice 'fspec paused this session but the pause could not be read' naming the reason, never silently dropped

examples.text: Bash call-1 running, get_pause_state tool_call_id None -> permission named Bash, no detail, no metadata (was: call-1's detail)

get_interaction_snapshot answers Err('interaction state unavailable') -> error notice 'fspec paused this session but the pause could not be read' with description 'interaction state unavailable', no permission
Snapshot pause kind 'Quadruple' -> error notice with description 'unknown fspec pause kind Quadruple'

architectureNotes.text: server/session.ts openPause attaches by transcript.toolCall(tool_call_id) only; transcript.runningToolCall removed; pauseState no longer swallows errors; getInteractionSnapshot Err throws; the Paused handler reports openPause failures with session.notice (severity error). server/interactions.ts parseInteractionSnapshot throws on an unknown pause kind.

FSPEC-060.title: Pick the fspec daemon serving the directory or fail naming the candidates
FSPEC-060.description: FSPEC-054 discovery prefers the live daemons/<pid>.json entry whose workspace holds the Paseo directory, then falls back to daemon.json and then to the lowest pid, so a directory no daemon serves silently reaches an arbitrary daemon. Replace the chain with one explicit rule: exactly one live entry must serve the directory (all live entries qualify for a client with no directory); none or several fail the connection with a message naming the candidates. FSPEC_DAEMON_URL / connectUrl stays the explicit override.

rules.text: An explicit connect URL (connectUrl option or FSPEC_DAEMON_URL) wins and skips discovery; it must be loopback

Discovery reads only the live daemons/<pid>.json entries beside daemon.json ($XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fspec/daemons or ~/.fspec/daemons); daemon.json is never read or removed; unreadable entries and entries of dead pids are not daemons

A client bound to a Paseo directory uses the one live daemon whose entry workspace holds the directory; a client bound to no directory (settings, catalog key without cwd) uses the one live daemon; no candidate or several candidates fail the connection with a message naming every live daemon (pid, workspace, port) and the way out (start fspec in the directory, stop all but one, or set FSPEC_DAEMON_URL)
The workspace registry is shared by every daemon using the same fspec data directory and each daemon records its start workspace there, so it cannot tell daemons apart and is not used for discovery
The provider's status() is available when an explicit URL is valid or at least one live daemon exists (it chooses none); a board panel no daemon serves reports the discovery reason for its directory

examples.text: daemons/100.json (/a, 4100) and daemons/200.json (/b, 4200): directory /b/web -> ws://127.0.0.1:4200/; directory /c -> error 'no fspec daemon serves /c — the live daemons are pid 100 in /a (port 4100), pid 200 in /b (port 4200); start fspec in /c, or set FSPEC_DAEMON_URL to choose a daemon'

daemons/100.json (/a) and daemons/300.json (/a/b): directory /a/b/c -> error '2 fspec daemons serve /a/b/c — pid 100 in /a (port 4100), pid 300 in /a/b (port 4300); stop all but one, or set FSPEC_DAEMON_URL to choose one'

Settings feed (no directory) with daemons /a and /b -> unavailable '2 fspec daemons are running and this connection serves no directory — …; set FSPEC_DAEMON_URL to choose one'; with only /a -> connects to /a

architectureNotes.text: server/daemon.ts: resolveTarget = explicit URL, else exactly one qualifying live entry (liveEntries over daemons/*.json); daemon.json resolution and stale-file removal removed; DaemonTarget.entryPath replaces daemonJsonPath, discoveryReadCount replaces readDaemonJsonCount; DaemonClientOptions.directory and bindDirectory(cwd) (first wins) replace preferWorkspace; status() checks availability without choosing. server/board.ts binds each panel directory, a failed discovery keeps a feed bound to that directory. server/provider.ts binds the catalog cache key's cwd. test/support/fake-daemon.ts tempHome writes daemons/4242.json (workspace /).

FSPEC-061.title: Open sessions only with an explicit or fspec default model
FSPEC-061.description: FSPEC-046 writes fspec's default model (set_default_model) when a fresh session opens on a daemon without one, and the catalog's default falls back to the first listed model, so Paseo silently picks a model and silently changes fspec's configuration. Remove the implicit write and the first-model default: a fresh session uses the chosen model or fspec's default model and fails with a clear message without one; a resumed session keeps its own model unless one is chosen; resetting an agent's model to the default without an fspec default fails clearly.

rules.text: The plugin never writes fspec's default model on its own: set_default_model is sent only from the providers screen's Default model row
The catalog's defaultModel is fspec's default model when the catalog lists it; otherwise the catalog has no default and no model is marked isDefault

A fresh session needs fspec's default model (fspec creates every session on it, handle_creation.rs / default_project.rs): without one the open fails before anything is created, telling the user to choose a model and set fspec's default; the session runs the chosen model, else fspec's default
A resumed session applies the chosen model, else its saved one; with neither it keeps the model fspec restored
Resetting an agent's model (configure model null) applies fspec's current default model; without one it fails 'fspec has no default model to reset to — choose a model'

examples.text: fspec default 'gone/old-model', catalog anthropic/claude-sonnet-4 and openai/gpt-5 -> catalog without defaultModel, no isDefault

No fspec default, open with model openai/gpt-5 -> fails 'fspec has no default model — fspec starts every session on its default model, so set one under fspec providers before opening openai/gpt-5'; no set_default_model, no create_session
No fspec default, open with no model -> fails 'fspec has no default model — choose a model for this agent and set fspec's default model under fspec providers'

architectureNotes.text: server/catalog.ts buildCatalog: defaultModel only when fspec's default is listed. server/session.ts open(): fresh sessions require get_default_model (two messages), no setDefaultModel; resumed sessions apply config.model ?? saved.model only; session.defaultModel removed; configure(model null) reads get_default_model.

FSPEC-062.title: Compare workspace paths through the real path of their deepest existing ancestor
FSPEC-062.description: within() (server/workspaces.ts) realpaths a path that exists but only resolve()s one that does not, so a directory not yet created under a symlinked spelling of a workspace (macOS /var vs /private/var) is compared unresolved against a resolved root and wrongly reported outside it; any realpath error was swallowed. Canonicalise both paths the same way: the deepest existing ancestor's real path plus the missing remainder; only ENOENT/ENOTDIR mean 'does not exist', any other failure is an error naming the path.

rules.text: within(root, dir) canonicalises both paths by one rule: the real path of the deepest existing ancestor with the not-yet-existing remainder appended
Only ENOENT and ENOTDIR from realpath mean the path does not exist; any other realpath failure throws 'cannot resolve <path>: <reason>'
A directory not yet created under a symlinked spelling of a workspace is inside that workspace

examples.text: Daemon workspace <tmp>/real (its real path), Paseo opens cwd <tmp>/link/new where link -> real and new does not exist -> create_session_checked in the start workspace and session.ready
within('<tmp>/real', '<tmp>/link/new/deeper') -> true; within('<tmp>/real', '<tmp>/other/new') -> false
realpath of a path inside an unreadable (mode 000) directory fails EACCES -> within throws 'cannot resolve <path>: ...'

architectureNotes.text: server/workspaces.ts canonicalPath: resolve(), realpathSync, on ENOENT/ENOTDIR recurse on dirname and join basename; the filesystem root always exists. Used by within() for discovery (server/daemon.ts), servingWorkspace (session.ts, board.ts).

FSPEC-063.title: Attach a sub-agent child only to the AgentManager spawn call whose result names it
FSPEC-063.description: openChild finds the parent's tool call by searching every tool output for the child's daemon id (transcript.toolCallMentioning), so a get_status/message/list result or a shell output that mentions the id becomes the child's toolCallId. fspec's explicit link is the AgentManager spawn result {"session_id":...} (AgentManagerResult::Spawned). Use only that; without it the child opens unattached. A failed get_supervisors lookup is logged, not swallowed.

rules.text: A child's toolCallId is the parent's AgentManager tool call whose input action is 'spawn' and whose result parses as a JSON object with session_id equal to the child's daemon session id (AgentManagerResult::Spawned, rust/tools/src/agent_manager/types.rs:209)
No tool output is searched for the id: another AgentManager action (message, get_status, list, close) or any other tool whose output mentions the id never links
Without that spawn call in the parent's transcript the child opens without toolCallId (unattached)
A failed get_supervisors lookup for an unknown daemon session is logged '[fspec] sub-agent lookup for <id> failed: <reason>' and the session is not adopted

examples.text: call-9 AgentManager {action:'spawn'} returns {"session_id": "sub-9"}, later call-10 AgentManager get_status returns text mentioning sub-9 -> child paseo-1:sub:sub-9 opens with toolCallId call-9
Only a Bash call whose output prints sub-9 -> child opens without toolCallId
get_supervisors for sub-9 rejects 'connection lost' -> logged, no session.opened

architectureNotes.text: server/transcript.ts: toolCallMentioning replaced by spawnCallOf(daemonSessionId) matching name AgentManager, input.action spawn, JSON output session_id. server/session.ts openChild uses it; adoptUnknown logs a failed getSupervisors through server/log.ts logFailure (console.error -> Paseo plugin log).

FSPEC-064.title: Fail the daemon connection on undecodable frames and require an explicit daemon URL port
FSPEC-064.description: server/daemon.ts ignores a binary frame whose envelope or rpc response frame cannot be decoded, ignores text frames silently, and an explicit connect URL without a port silently dials 80/443 (wss is silently rewritten to ws and the path dropped). An undecodable frame is a protocol error: log it, close the socket and drop the connection with the reason, like the daemon's pump (rust/rpc-server/src/pump.rs:139-145). Text frames are logged and ignored (pump.rs:181-183). An explicit URL must be ws://, name a port and the / path, or the connection fails naming the URL.

rules.text: A binary frame whose Envelope does not decode, or an Rpc envelope whose tarpc response frame does not decode, is a protocol error: it is logged, the socket is closed and the connection drops with reason 'protocol error: <the envelope|an rpc response> frame could not be decoded — <decoder message>' (as fspec's pump closes on an undecodable envelope, rust/rpc-server/src/pump.rs:139-145)

After a protocol error, outstanding requests reject with the reason, open sessions get session.runtime_failed naming it (the FSPEC-030 lost-connection path) and later frames of that socket are not processed; during the handshake the connect fails with it
A text frame is logged and ignored, as fspec's pump does (pump.rs:181-183); a frame of any other non-binary type is a protocol error

An explicit connect URL must be ws://<loopback host>:<port>/ — no port fails '<url> names no port — the fspec daemon has no default port; use ws://127.0.0.1:<port>/'; another scheme or a path other than / fails naming the URL; nothing is defaulted or rewritten
A response for a request id nobody waits for is logged

examples.text: Established connection, the daemon sends the bytes ff ff ff ff -> in-flight list_providers rejects 'fspec daemon connection was lost: protocol error: the envelope frame could not be decoded — ...', the client is connection-lost, the plugin log has the reason
During the handshake an rpc envelope carries an undecodable response frame -> connect() rejects with the protocol error and the socket is closed

FSPEC_DAEMON_URL=ws://127.0.0.1/ -> status unavailable 'fspec daemon connect URL ws://127.0.0.1/ names no port — the fspec daemon has no default port; use ws://127.0.0.1:<port>/'; wss://127.0.0.1:5555/ and ws://127.0.0.1:5555/fspec-read-v2 fail naming the URL; ws://127.0.0.1:80/ is port 80

architectureNotes.text: server/daemon.ts attachSocket onMessage/onFrame: a per-socket dropped flag; protocolError() logs (server/log.ts), rejects the handshake or handleDrop(reason), then closes the socket with 1002 without a second connection-lost; toBytes distinguishes text frames; resolveTarget validates scheme, explicit port (read from the raw authority, since URL elides :80) and path.

FSPEC-065.title: Surface catalog-key, post-write refresh and sign-in polling failures in provider settings
FSPEC-065.description: catalogCacheKey answers no key on any error; runWrite swallows reload/refresh failures after a successful write; the OAuth sheet retries a failed status poll silently forever, swallows a failed copy and a failed cancel. Propagate the catalog-key error (Paseo shows the provider in error), report post-write refresh failures as the write's warning, end the sign-in on a failed poll with its reason, show copy failures and log cancel failures.

rules.text: getCatalogCacheKey rejects with the reason when the key cannot be derived: the discovery/connection error itself, or 'fspec daemon list_provider_credentials failed: <error>'; Paseo then shows the fspec provider in error with that message (provider-snapshot-manager.ts:928-948)

After a successful settings write, a failed reload of the provider list adds the warning 'Saved, but the provider list could not be reloaded: <reason>' and a failed Paseo model refresh adds 'Saved, but Paseo's fspec models could not be refreshed: <reason>'; they follow the write's own warning, one per line, and the outcome stays ok
A sign-in status poll that fails ends the sign-in as failed with 'The sign-in status could not be read: <reason>' instead of retrying silently
A failed copy of the device code shows 'The code could not be copied: <reason>' on the sheet; a failed cancel when the sheet closes is logged to the console

examples.text: No fspec daemon running -> getCatalogCacheKey rejects 'no fspec daemon is running — no live entry in <dir>; start fspec daemon first'
Saving a Gemini key succeeds, reload rejects 'socket closed' -> { ok: true, warning: 'Saved, but the provider list could not be reloaded: socket closed' }
Device sign-in pending, the status RPC rejects 'request timed out' -> failed 'The sign-in status could not be read: request timed out'

architectureNotes.text: server/provider.ts catalogCacheKey throws. client/settings-actions.ts runWrite collects refresh warnings. New client/oauth-flow.ts (pure): watchSignIn(status, current), copyCode(copy, code), cancelOnClose(cancel, loginId) used by client/oauth-sheet.tsx.

FSPEC-066.title: Tell an unserved directory from a failed board check and open agents only on fspec's default model
FSPEC-066.description: fspec.board.available answers false on any error, and the client turns a failed RPC into false too, so a broken daemon looks like an unserved directory. Answer served / unserved (no daemon or no workspace serves it) / failed (anything else) and show failures. Open in agent falls back to the first listed model when none is the default and treats a Paseo listModels error as no models: use only fspec's default model and surface listModels errors. The workspace subscription release error is logged.

rules.text: fspec.board.available answers { state: 'served' }, { state: 'unserved', reason } or { state: 'failed', error }

Unserved: discovery finds no daemon for the directory (no live entry, or none whose workspace holds it — DaemonNotFoundError from server/daemon.ts), or the daemon's workspaces hold none for it; every other error (several daemons, connection, list_workspaces error, unreadable daemons directory, plugin unloaded) is failed

The client gives served workspaces the 'fspec board' header button, unserved ones none, and a failed check (including a failed RPC) is logged '[fspec board] availability check for <dir> failed: <error>' and shows the button titled 'fspec board (error)', whose panel reports the failure

Open in agent creates the agent only on the model Paseo marks default (fspec's default model); without one it fails 'fspec has no default model — set one under fspec providers'; never the first listed model
Paseo's listModels error fails Open in agent with that error; a response without models fails 'Paseo listed no fspec models'
A failed release of the workspace subscription is logged

examples.text: Daemon serves /ws: available /ws/sub -> served; /other -> unserved 'the fspec daemon serves /ws, not /other — ...'; list_workspaces errors 'registry unreadable' -> failed 'fspec daemon list_workspaces failed: registry unreadable'
No daemon running -> unserved 'no fspec daemon is running — ...'
Models m1, m2 with none default -> Open in agent fails 'fspec has no default model — set one under fspec providers', no agent created
listModels answers { error: 'provider fspec is loading' } -> Open in agent fails 'provider fspec is loading'

architectureNotes.text: shared/board.ts boardAvailableRpc output becomes a discriminated union. server/daemon.ts exports DaemonNotFoundError (noDaemon and the none-serves case). server/board.ts both available() implementations. client/board-buttons.ts deps.available returns the union. client/open-in-agent.ts openInAgent default-only + fspecModels(result) used by client/board-panel.tsx. client/register.ts logs the release failure.

FSPEC-067.title: Report every failed background daemon call of a session
FSPEC-067.description: server/session.ts swallows failures of set_active_session, interrupt, the cleanup destroy of a half-opened session, list_checkpoints, get_work_unit_focus, checkpoint attachment, the steer's deny reply, a child's clear_active_session, sub-agent destroys and the prompt search. Each failure is logged and, where the user is affected, shown as a session notice or fails the request; a failed cleanup never hides the original error.

rules.text: A failed background daemon call of a session is logged '[fspec] <what> (<paseo session>): <reason>' and, while the session is open, shown as a warning session.notice titled <what> with the reason

set_active_session (markActive), get_work_unit_focus (an RPC failure or an error result), list_checkpoints after an fspec call and the steer's deny reply (an RPC failure or an error result; the request then stays shown) are reported that way
A sub-agent child's get_active_session/clear_active_session failure is reported on its parent
session.interrupt sends interrupt before request.completed; a failure answers request.failed
list_checkpoints is read before any daemon session is created; a failure fails the open and creates nothing
A failed cleanup destroy after a failed open keeps the original error first: '<original>; the fspec session <id> it created could not be destroyed: <reason>'
Closing a session still destroys and closes it when sub-agent lookups or destroys fail, then answers request.failed 'fspec could not destroy every sub-agent of this session: <id>: <reason>; ...'
A failed persistence_search_history fails the import list with 'fspec daemon persistence_search_history failed: <reason>'
can_stop_runtime read failures and connection-close destroy failures are logged; can_stop_runtime still answers false

examples.text: set_active_session rejects 'board busy' on open -> notice 'fspec could not mark this session active on its board' / description containing 'board busy'
interrupt rejects 'Session not found' -> request.failed with it, no request.completed

set_session_model fails 'unknown model' and destroy_session then fails 'busy' -> open fails 'fspec daemon set_session_model failed: unknown model; the fspec session fspec-sess-42 it created could not be destroyed: fspec daemon destroy_session failed: busy'
sub-9 destroy fails 'busy' -> fspec-sess-42 destroyed, session.closed, request.failed 'fspec could not destroy every sub-agent of this session: sub-9: fspec daemon destroy_session failed: busy'
persistence_search_history answers Err('history unavailable') -> the list fails 'fspec daemon persistence_search_history failed: history unavailable'

architectureNotes.text: server/session.ts: report(session, what, error) via server/log.ts logFailure + session.notice; subordinateTree returns { order, failure }; destroySubordinates returns failure descriptions; open() reads list_checkpoints first; interrupt awaits before completing. New feature spec/features/fspec-session-failure-reports.feature; fspec-session-search, fspec-subordinate-close, fspec-session-lifecycle and fspec-idle-runtime scenarios updated.

FSPEC-068.title: Decode transcript entries and interaction snapshots strictly
FSPEC-068.description: server/transcript-json.ts and server/interactions.ts default every missing or mistyped field of daemon JSON to an empty string, 0, an empty list, info severity or a user interruption, and map an unknown Paseo action or a missing HITL answer object to a guessed reply. Decode the serde shapes exactly (rpc-types stream_chunk.rs, chunk_support.rs, background_session/interactions.rs) and fail with the field that is wrong.
